bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 起閼逢執徐，盡著雍涒灘，凡五年。

translations.literal: Beginning in the year Qimao (the thirty-fifth year of the sexagenary cycle), and ending in Zhuoyong (the thirty-eighth year), in all five years.
translations.idiomatic: The period covered runs from the Qimao year of the cycle through Zhuoyong, five years in all.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，甲子，日有食之。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, on the day jiazi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring, on the first day of the first month (jiazi), a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 2己巳，隋主享太廟；

translations.literal: 2 On the day jisi, the Sui emperor offered sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple;
translations.idiomatic: 2 On jisi, Emperor Wen of Sui performed the ancestral rites at the Imperial Temple;

sentences.zh: 辛未，祀南郊。

translations.literal: on the day xinwei, he sacrificed at the Southern Altar.
translations.idiomatic: on xinwei he offered sacrifice at the Southern Altar.

sentences.zh: 壬申，梁主入朝於隋，服通天冠、絳紗袍，北面受郊勞。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, the Liang ruler came to court at Sui wearing the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe, facing north to receive the suburban greeting.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the Liang emperor came to the Sui court in the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe, facing north to receive the greeting prescribed for the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 及入見於大興殿，隋主服通天冠、絳紗袍，梁主服遠遊冠、朝服，君臣並拜。

translations.literal: When he entered to have an audience in the Daxing Hall, the Sui emperor wore the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe, the Liang ruler wore the Yuanyou crown and court dress, and ruler and subject bowed to each other.
translations.idiomatic: When he was received in the Hall of Great Prosperity, the Sui emperor wore the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe while the Liang ruler wore the traveling crown and court robes; the two rulers exchanged bows as equals.

sentences.zh: 賜縑萬匹，珍玩稱是。

translations.literal: He was granted ten thousand bolts of silk, and curios in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: He was given ten thousand bolts of silk and a comparable array of precious objects.

sentences.zh: 隋前華州刺史張賓、儀同三司劉暉等造《甲子元歷》成，奏之。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin, former governor of Hua Province in Sui, Liu Hui of the third rank of ceremonial parity, and others completed the Jiazi Primordial Calendar and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin, formerly governor of Hua Province under Sui, Liu Hui, a third-rank ceremonial peer, and others finished the Jiazi Primordial Calendar and submitted it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，詔頒新歷。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, an edict ordered the promulgation of the new calendar.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen an edict ordered the new calendar to be issued throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 3癸巳，大赦。

translations.literal: 3 On the day guisi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: 3 On guisi a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 4二月，乙巳，隋主餞梁主於灞上。

translations.literal: 4 In the second month, on the day yisi, the Sui emperor gave a farewell feast for the Liang ruler at Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: 4 In the second month, on yisi, Emperor Wen of Sui gave a farewell banquet for the Liang emperor at Bashang.

sentences.zh: 突厥蘇尼部男女萬餘口降隋。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand men and women of the Suni division of the Turks submitted to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand men and women of the Turkish Suni tribe surrendered to Sui.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，隋主如隴州。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, the Sui emperor went to Long Province.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the Sui emperor traveled to Long Province.

sentences.zh: 突厥達頭可汗請降於隋。

translations.literal: Tatou, khan of the Turks, requested to submit to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Tatou Khan of the Turks asked to surrender to Sui.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚子，隋以吏部尚書虞慶則為右僕射。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day gengzi, Sui appointed Yu Qingze, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month on gengzi, Sui named Yu Qingze, Minister of Personnel, Right Vice Premier.

sentences.zh: 隋上大將軍賀婁子干發五州兵擊吐谷渾，殺男女萬餘口，二旬而還。

translations.literal: The Sui Grand General Helou Zigan mobilized troops from five provinces to attack the Tuyuhun, killed more than ten thousand men and women, and returned within twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Grand General Helou Zigan raised troops from five provinces, struck the Tuyuhun, killed more than ten thousand people, and returned within twenty days.

sentences.zh: 帝以隴西頻被寇掠，而俗不設村塢，命子干勒民為堡，仍營田積穀。

translations.literal: Because Longxi had repeatedly been raided and the custom there was not to build walled villages, the emperor ordered Zigan to compel the people to build forts and also to open fields and store grain.
translations.idiomatic: Because Longxi had suffered repeated raids and the local custom was not to build fortified villages, the emperor ordered Zigan to compel the people to erect forts while also farming fields and stockpiling grain.

sentences.zh: 子幹上書曰：「隴右、河西，土曠民稀，邊境未寧，不可廣佃。

translations.literal: Zigan submitted a memorial saying: "Longyou and Hexi have broad lands and sparse population; the frontier is not yet secure, and extensive cultivation cannot be undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: Zigan wrote to the throne: "In Longyou and Hexi the land is vast and the people few; the border is still unsettled, and large-scale farming is impracticable.

sentences.zh: 比見屯田之所，獲少費多，虛役人功，卒逢踐暴；

translations.literal: Recently I have seen that at garrison-farm sites the yield is small and the cost great, labor is wasted in vain, and in the end the crops are trampled and destroyed;
translations.idiomatic: Lately I have seen garrison farms yield little while costing much, waste labor in vain, and in the end have their crops trampled underfoot;

sentences.zh: 屯田疏遠者請皆廢省。

translations.literal: I request that all distant garrison farms be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that remote garrison farms be abolished entirely.

sentences.zh: 但隴右之人以畜牧為事，若更屯聚，彌不自安。

translations.literal: But the people of Longyou make their living by herding; if they are further gathered into settlements, they will be even less at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Longyou live by herding; if they are forced into settlements they will only grow more uneasy.

sentences.zh: 但使鎮戍連接，烽堠相望，民雖散居，必謂無慮。」

translations.literal: Only let the garrison posts link together and beacon towers look out upon one another; though the people live scattered, they will surely feel secure."
translations.idiomatic: If only the garrisons are linked and beacon towers keep watch on one another, the people may live scattered yet still feel safe."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 以子幹曉習邊事，丁巳，以為榆關總管。

translations.literal: Because Zigan was well versed in frontier affairs, on the day dingsi he was made overall commander of Yuguan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zigan knew the border country well, on dingsi he was appointed overall commander at Yuguan Pass.

sentences.zh: 5五月，以吏部尚書江總為僕射。

translations.literal: 5 In the fifth month, Jiang Zong, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, was made Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: 5 In the fifth month Jiang Zong, Minister of Personnel, was appointed Vice Premier.

sentences.zh: 6隋主以渭水多沙，深淺不常，漕者苦之，六月，壬子，詔太子左庶子宇文愷帥水工鑿渠，引渭水，自大興城東至潼關三百餘里，名曰廣通渠。

translations.literal: 6 Because the Wei River had much sand and its depth was not constant, causing hardship to those who transported grain by water, in the sixth month, on the day renzi, the Sui emperor ordered the Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent Yuwen Kai to lead water engineers in cutting a canal to draw off the Wei, from east of Daxing city to Tong Pass, more than three hundred li, named the Guangtong Canal.
translations.idiomatic: 6 Because the Wei River was sandy and its depth unpredictable, making transport by water arduous, in the sixth month on renzi the Sui emperor ordered Yuwen Kai, Left Assistant to the Crown Prince, to lead hydraulic engineers in cutting a canal to divert the Wei from east of Daxing to Tong Pass, more than three hundred li in length, called the Guangtong Canal.

sentences.zh: 漕運通利，關內賴之。

translations.literal: Grain transport became convenient, and the lands within the Pass relied upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Grain transport ran smoothly, and the Guanzhong region came to depend on it.

sentences.zh: 7秋，七月，丙寅，遣兼散騎常侍謝泉等聘於隋。

translations.literal: 7 In autumn, the seventh month, on the day bingyin, he dispatched the concurrent Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Xie Quan and others on a mission of friendship to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: 7 In autumn, in the seventh month on bingyin, he sent Xie Quan, concurrent Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and others on a friendly mission to Sui.

sentences.zh: 8八月，壬寅，隋鄧恭竇熾卒。

translations.literal: 8 In the eighth month, on the day renyin, Deng Gong Dou Chi of Sui died.
translations.idiomatic: 8 In the eighth month, on renyin, Dou Chi, Duke of Deng, died in Sui.

sentences.zh: 9乙卯，將軍夏侯苗請降於隋，隋主以通和，不納。

translations.literal: 9 On the day yimao, the general Xiahou Miao requested to surrender to Sui; the Sui emperor, because relations were friendly, did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: 9 On yimao General Xiahou Miao offered to defect to Sui, but the Sui emperor, wishing to preserve friendly relations, refused to accept.

sentences.zh: 10九月，甲戌，隋主以關中饑，行如洛陽。

translations.literal: 10 In the ninth month, on the day jiaxu, because Guanzhong was suffering famine, the Sui emperor traveled to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: 10 In the ninth month, on jiaxu, famine in Guanzhong drove the Sui emperor to travel to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 11隋主不喜詞華，詔天下公私文翰並宜實錄。

translations.literal: 11 The Sui emperor disliked ornate rhetoric and decreed that all public and private documents throughout the realm should record facts plainly.
translations.idiomatic: 11 The Sui emperor disliked flowery language and decreed that all official and private writing in the realm should record facts plainly.

sentences.zh: 泗州刺史司馬幼之，文表華艷，付所司治罪。

translations.literal: Sima Youzhi, governor of Si Province, wrote memorials of florid elegance and was handed over to the appropriate office for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Youzhi, governor of Si Province, submitted florid memorials and was handed over to the authorities for punishment.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史趙郡李諤亦以當時屬文，體尚輕薄。

translations.literal: Li E of Zhao Commandery, Attending Secretary in the Office for Drafting Imperial Documents, also held that the literary compositions of the time were still inclined to frivolity.
translations.idiomatic: Li E of Zhao, Attending Secretary in the Office for Drafting Imperial Documents, likewise held that contemporary writing still favored frivolous style.

sentences.zh: 上書曰：「魏之三祖，崇尚文詞，忽君人之大道，好彫蟲之藝。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "The three ancestors of Wei esteemed literary ornament, neglected the great Way of rulership, and delighted in the art of carving insects.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to the throne: "The three founders of Wei exalted literary ornament, neglected the great duties of rulership, and delighted in trivial word-craft.

sentences.zh: 下之從上，遂成風俗。

translations.literal: Those below followed those above, and it became custom.
translations.idiomatic: Those below imitated those above until it became custom.

sentences.zh: 江左、齊、梁，其弊彌甚：競一韻之奇，爭一字之巧；

translations.literal: In the lands south of the Yangzi, Qi, and Liang the abuse grew worse still: they vied for the marvel of a single rhyme and contended for the cleverness of a single character;
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangzi, under Qi and Liang, the abuse grew worse still: writers vied for a single striking rhyme and fought over the cleverness of a single character;

sentences.zh: 連篇累牘，不出月露之形，積案盈箱，唯是風雲之狀。

translations.literal: page after page never departed from the shapes of moon and dew; piled desks and overflowing boxes contained only images of wind and clouds.
translations.idiomatic: page after page never rose above images of moon and dew; piled desks and overflowing boxes held nothing but descriptions of wind and clouds.

sentences.zh: 世俗以此相高，朝廷據茲擢士。

translations.literal: The world took this as a mark of esteem, and the court promoted men on this basis.
translations.idiomatic: Society esteemed this above all else, and the court promoted officials on that basis.

sentences.zh: 祿利之路既開，愛尚之情愈篤。

translations.literal: Once the path to salary and profit was opened, the passion for it grew ever more ardent.
translations.idiomatic: Once the path to salary and profit lay open, devotion to such writing grew ever more intense.

sentences.zh: 於是閭裡童昏，貴游總草，未窺六甲，先制五言。

translations.literal: Thus village children and noble scions alike, before they had mastered the six jia, already composed five-character verse.
translations.idiomatic: Thus village children and noble scions alike composed five-character verse before they had even mastered the six jia.

sentences.zh: 至如羲皇、舜、禹之典，伊、傅、周、孔之說，不復關心，何嘗入耳。

translations.literal: As for the classics of Fuxi, Shun, and Yu, and the teachings of Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius, they no longer cared for them and never let them enter their ears.
translations.idiomatic: The classics of Fuxi, Shun, and Yu, and the teachings of Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius no longer interested them and never reached their ears.

sentences.zh: 以傲誕為清虛，以緣情為勳績，指儒素為古拙，用詞賦為君子。

translations.literal: They took arrogance and extravagance for purity and emptiness, emotional indulgence for merit, called plain Confucian conduct antiquated and crude, and made rhapsodic verse the mark of a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: They took arrogance and extravagance for refinement, emotional indulgence for achievement, called plain Confucian conduct old-fashioned, and made rhapsodic verse the mark of a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 故文筆日繁，其政日亂，良由棄大聖之軌模，構無用以為用也。

translations.literal: Therefore literary composition grew daily more elaborate and government daily more chaotic, truly because they abandoned the great sage's model and built useless things into their standard of use.
translations.idiomatic: Thus writing grew ever more elaborate and government ever more chaotic, precisely because they abandoned the great sage's model and made the useless their standard of worth.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷雖有是詔，如聞外州遠縣，仍踵弊風：躬仁孝之行者，擯落私門，下加收齒；

translations.literal: Now although the court has issued such a decree, I hear that distant prefectures and counties still follow the old abuse: those who personally practiced benevolence and filial piety were cast out at private gates and taxed for their coming of age below;
translations.idiomatic: Although the court has issued such a decree, I hear that distant prefectures and counties still follow the old abuse: men who practiced benevolence and filial piety were turned away at their gates and taxed for coming of age;

sentences.zh: 工輕薄之藝者，選充吏職，舉送天朝。

translations.literal: those skilled in frivolous arts were selected for office and recommended to the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: those skilled in frivolous arts were selected for office and sent up to the capital.

sentences.zh: 蓋由刺史、縣令未遵風教。

translations.literal: This was because prefects and magistrates did not follow the wind of instruction.
translations.idiomatic: This was because prefects and magistrates did not enforce the court's teaching.

sentences.zh: 請普加采察，送台推劾。」

translations.literal: I request that investigation be broadly applied and offenders sent to the Censorate for impeachment."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that investigations be conducted everywhere and offenders sent to the Censorate for prosecution."

sentences.zh: 又上言：「士大夫矜伐干進，無復廉恥，乞明加罪黜，以懲風軌。」

translations.literal: He further submitted: "Scholar-officials boast and strive for advancement without any sense of shame; I beg that punishment and dismissal be clearly imposed to correct public morals."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Scholar-officials boast and scramble for advancement without shame; I beg that clear punishments and dismissals be imposed to restore public morals."

sentences.zh: 詔以諤前後所奏頒示四方。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that Li E's successive memorials be promulgated throughout the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Li E's successive memorials promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 12突厥沙缽略可汗數為隋所敗，乃請和親。

translations.literal: 12 Shabolue Khan of the Turks had been repeatedly defeated by Sui and therefore requested a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: 12 Shabolue Khan of the Turks, having been defeated repeatedly by Sui, sought a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 千金公主自請改姓楊氏，為隋主女。

translations.literal: Princess Qianjin herself requested to change her surname to Yang and become a daughter of the Sui emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Qianjin herself asked to take the surname Yang and be recognized as a daughter of the Sui emperor.

sentences.zh: 隋主遣開府儀同三司徐平和使於沙缽略，更封千金公主為大義公主。

translations.literal: The Sui emperor sent Xu Pinghe, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with ceremonial parity of the third rank, as envoy to Shabolue and re-enfeoffed Princess Qianjin as Princess Dayi.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor sent Xu Pinghe, a third-rank ceremonial peer, as envoy to Shabolue and re-enfeoffed Princess Qianjin as Princess Dayi.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣請因釁乘之，隋主不許。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Yang Guang requested to take advantage of the opening to strike, but the Sui emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jin Yang Guang asked to seize the opportunity to attack, but the Sui emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略遣使致書曰：「從天生大突厥天下賢聖天子伊利居盧設莫何沙缽略可汗致書大隋皇帝：皇帝，婦父，乃是翁比。

translations.literal: Shabolue sent an envoy with a letter saying: "I, Shabolue Khan, Heaven-born Great Turk, sage and holy Son of Heaven over all the world, Ilugur Shemohe, write to the Great Sui Emperor: The Emperor is my wife's father and is like a grandfather to me.
translations.idiomatic: Shabolue sent an envoy with a letter: "I, Shabolue Khan, Heaven-born Great Turk, sage and holy ruler of all under heaven, Ilugur Shemohe, write to the Great Sui Emperor: You are my wife's father and stand to me as a grandfather.

sentences.zh: 此為女夫，乃是兒例。

translations.literal: As her husband I am like a son.
translations.idiomatic: As her husband I stand to you as a son.

sentences.zh: 兩境雖殊，情義如一。

translations.literal: Though our two realms differ, our affection is one.
translations.idiomatic: Though our two realms differ, our bond is one.

sentences.zh: 自今子子孫孫，乃至萬世，親好不絕。

translations.literal: From now, sons and grandsons, even unto ten thousand generations, our kinship and friendship shall not cease.
translations.idiomatic: From now through sons and grandsons, even for ten thousand generations, our kinship and friendship shall not end.

sentences.zh: 上天為證，終不違負！

translations.literal: Heaven be witness—I shall never break faith!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven be witness—I shall never break faith!

sentences.zh: 此國羊馬，皆皇帝之畜。

translations.literal: The sheep and horses of this land are all the Emperor's herds.
translations.idiomatic: The sheep and horses of this land are all yours, Emperor.

sentences.zh: 彼之繒彩，皆此國之物。」

translations.literal: The silks and brocades over there are all goods of this land."
translations.idiomatic: The silks and brocades on your side are all goods of this land."

sentences.zh: 帝復書曰：「大隋天子貽書大突厥沙缽略可汗：得書，知大有善意。

translations.literal: The emperor replied with a letter saying: "The Great Sui Son of Heaven sends a letter to Shabolue Khan of the Great Turks: Having received your letter, I know you have great goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote back: "The Great Sui Son of Heaven sends this letter to Shabolue Khan of the Great Turks: I have received your letter and know that your goodwill is great.

sentences.zh: 既為沙缽略婦翁，今日視沙缽略與兒子不異。

translations.literal: Since I am Shabolue's father-in-law, from this day I regard Shabolue as no different from a son.
translations.idiomatic: As Shabolue's father-in-law, from this day I regard him as no different from a son.

sentences.zh: 時遣大臣往彼省女，復省沙缽略也。」

translations.literal: I shall presently send a great minister there to visit my daughter and also to visit Shabolue."
translations.idiomatic: I shall presently send a great minister to visit my daughter and Shabolue as well."

sentences.zh: 於是遣尚書右僕射虞慶則使於沙缽略，車騎將軍長孫晟副之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Yu Qingze, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, as envoy to Shabolue, with General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhangsun Sheng as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he sent Right Vice Premier Yu Qingze as envoy to Shabolue, with General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhangsun Sheng as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略陳兵列其珍寶，坐見慶則，稱病不能起，且曰：「我諸父以來，不向人拜。」

translations.literal: Shabolue arrayed his troops and displayed his treasures, sat to receive Qingze, claimed illness and could not rise, and said: "Since the time of my fathers' generation, I have not bowed to anyone."
translations.idiomatic: Shabolue drew up his troops, displayed his treasures, and received Qingze seated, claiming illness and refusing to rise, saying: "Since my fathers' time I have bowed to no one."

sentences.zh: 慶則責而諭之。

translations.literal: Qingze rebuked him and instructed him.
translations.idiomatic: Qingze rebuked him and lectured him.

sentences.zh: 千金公主私謂慶則曰：「可汗豺狼性；

translations.literal: Princess Qianjin privately told Qingze: "The khan has the nature of a wolf;
translations.idiomatic: Princess Qianjin told Qingze privately: "The khan has a wolf's nature;

sentences.zh: 過與爭，將嚙人。」

translations.literal: if you contend with him too far, he will bite."
translations.idiomatic: if you push him too hard, he will bite."

sentences.zh: 長孫晟謂沙缽略曰：「突厥與隋俱大國天子，可汗不起，安敢違意！

translations.literal: Zhangsun Sheng said to Shabolue: "Turks and Sui are both great realms with Sons of Heaven; if the khan does not rise, how dare we go against his intent!
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Sheng said to Shabolue: "Turks and Sui are both great powers ruled by Sons of Heaven; if you do not rise, how dare we defy the emperor's will!

sentences.zh: 但可賀敦為帝女，則可汗是大隋女婿，奈何不敬婦翁！」

translations.literal: But since Kehedun is the Emperor's daughter, the khan is the Great Sui's son-in-law—how can you fail to respect your wife's father!"
translations.idiomatic: But Kehedun is the emperor's daughter, so you are the Great Sui's son-in-law—how can you fail to honor your father-in-law!"

sentences.zh: 沙缽略笑謂其達官曰：「須拜婦翁！」

translations.literal: Shabolue laughed and said to his high officials: "I must bow to my wife's father!"
translations.idiomatic: Shabolue laughed and told his high officials: "I must bow to my father-in-law!"

sentences.zh: 乃起拜頓顙，跪受璽書，以戴於首，既而大慚，與群下相聚慟哭。

translations.literal: Thereupon he rose, bowed with his forehead to the ground, knelt to receive the imperial letter, placed it on his head, and afterward was deeply ashamed and wept together with his followers.
translations.idiomatic: He then rose, kowtowed, knelt to receive the imperial letter and placed it on his head; afterward, deeply ashamed, he wept together with his followers.

sentences.zh: 慶則又遣稱臣，沙缽略謂左右曰：「何謂臣？」

translations.literal: Qingze further had him styled a subject; Shabolue asked those beside him: "What does 'subject' mean?"
translations.idiomatic: Qingze further had him address himself as a subject; Shabolue asked his attendants: "What does 'subject' mean?"

sentences.zh: 左右曰：「隋言臣，猶此雲奴耳。」

translations.literal: Those beside him said: "In Sui speech 'subject' is like our word 'slave.'"
translations.idiomatic: They said: "In Sui speech 'subject' means the same as our word 'slave.'"

sentences.zh: 沙缽略曰：「得為大隋天子奴，虞僕射之力也。」

translations.literal: Shabolue said: "To become a slave of the Great Sui Son of Heaven—that is Vice Director Yu's doing."
translations.idiomatic: Shabolue said: "To become a slave of the Great Sui Son of Heaven—that is Vice Premier Yu's doing."

sentences.zh: 贈慶則馬千匹，並以從妹妻之。

translations.literal: He gave Qingze a thousand horses and also gave him a younger cousin in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Qingze a thousand horses and married him to a younger cousin of his own.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，壬戌，隋主遣兼散騎常侍薛道衡等來聘，戒道衡「當識朕意，勿以言辭相折。」

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on the day renxu, the Sui emperor sent the concurrent Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Xue Daoheng and others on a mission of friendship, admonishing Daoheng: "You must understand my intent and not try to overcome them with rhetoric."
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the eleventh month on renxu, the Sui emperor sent Xue Daoheng, concurrent Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and others on a friendly mission, instructing Daoheng: "You must understand my intent and not try to best them in debate."

sentences.zh: 13是歲，上於光昭殿前起臨春、結綺、望仙三閣，各高數十丈，連延數十間，其窗、牖、壁帶、縣楣、欄、檻皆以沈、檀為之，飾以金玉，間以珠翠，外施珠簾，內有寶床、寶帳，其服玩瑰麗，近古所未有。

translations.literal: 13 That year the emperor built before the Hall of Bright Radiance the three towers Linchun, Jieqi, and Wangxian, each several tens of zhang high and extending for several tens of bays; their windows, lattices, wall bands, hanging beams, railings, and balustrades were all made of aloeswood and sandalwood, adorned with gold and jade and set with pearls and kingfisher feathers; pearl curtains hung outside, and inside were precious couches and canopies; their furnishings were so magnificent that nothing like them had been seen in recent antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: 13 That year the emperor built before the Hall of Bright Radiance the three towers Linchun, Jieqi, and Wangxian, each several tens of zhang high and extending for dozens of bays; windows, lattices, wall bands, beams, railings, and balustrades were all of aloeswood and sandalwood, adorned with gold, jade, pearls, and kingfisher feathers; pearl curtains hung outside, and inside were precious couches and canopies—furnishings so magnificent that nothing like them had been seen in recent memory.

sentences.zh: 每微風暫至，香聞數里。

translations.literal: Whenever a slight breeze passed, the fragrance could be smelled for several li.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a light breeze stirred, the fragrance could be smelled for miles.

sentences.zh: 其下積石為山，引水為池，雜植奇花異卉。

translations.literal: Below them stones were piled into hills, water was drawn to form pools, and rare flowers and exotic plants were planted in profusion.
translations.idiomatic: Below them stones were piled into hills, channels drew water into pools, and rare flowers and exotic plants were planted throughout.

sentences.zh: 上自居臨春閣，張貴妃居結綺閣，龔、孔二貴嬪居望仙閣，並復道交相往來。

translations.literal: The emperor himself dwelt in the Linchun Tower, Consort Zhang in the Jieqi Tower, and the two honored ladies Gong and Kong in the Wangxian Tower, with covered walkways linking them so they could visit one another.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lived in the Linchun Tower, Consort Zhang in the Jieqi Tower, and Honored Ladies Gong and Kong in the Wangxian Tower, linked by covered walkways so they could visit one another.

sentences.zh: 又有王、李二美人，張、薛二淑媛，袁昭儀、何婕妤、江脩容，並有寵，迭游其上。

translations.literal: There were also the two beauties Wang and Li, the two fair ladies Zhang and Xue, Lady Yuan the Zhaoyi, Lady He the Jieyu, and Lady Jiang the Xiurong, all favored, who took turns roaming upon the towers.
translations.idiomatic: The beauties Wang and Li, the fair ladies Zhang and Xue, Lady Yuan the Zhaoyi, Lady He the Jieyu, and Lady Jiang the Xiurong were all favored and took turns visiting the towers.

sentences.zh: 以宮人有文學者袁大捨等為女學士。

translations.literal: Palace women of literary accomplishment such as Yuan Dashe were made female academicians.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women of literary accomplishment such as Yuan Dashe were appointed female academicians.

sentences.zh: 僕射江總雖為宰輔，不親政務，日與都官尚書孔范、散騎常侍王瑳等文士十餘人，侍上游宴後庭，無復尊卑之序，謂之「狎客」。

translations.literal: Although Vice Director Jiang Zong was chief minister, he did not attend to government affairs; day after day he and more than ten literary men such as Kong Fan, Minister of the Capital Office, and Wang Chao, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, attended the emperor in feasting and revelry in the rear palace, with no regard for rank and precedence, and were called "intimate guests."
translations.idiomatic: Although Vice Premier Jiang Zong was chief minister, he neglected government; day after day he and more than ten literati such as Kong Fan, Minister of the Capital Office, and Wang Chao, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, attended the emperor in feasting in the rear palace without regard for rank, and were called "intimate guests."

sentences.zh: 上每飲酒，使諸妃、嬪及女學士與狎客共賦詩，互相贈答，采其尤艷麗者，被以新聲，選宮女千餘人習而歌之，分部迭進。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor drank wine, he had the various consorts, ladies, and female academicians compose poetry together with the intimate guests, exchanging verses; the most florid and beautiful were set to new music, and more than a thousand palace women were chosen to learn and sing them, entering in groups by turns.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor drank, he had consorts, ladies, and female academicians compose poetry with the intimate guests and exchange verses; the most florid were set to new music, and more than a thousand palace women learned and sang them, entering in groups by turns.

sentences.zh: 其曲有《玉樹後庭花》、《臨春樂》等，大略皆美諸妃嬪之容色。

translations.literal: Among the songs were "Jade Tree in the Rear Court" and "Linchun Joy," which for the most part praised the beauty of the various consorts and ladies.
translations.idiomatic: Among the songs were "Jade Tree in the Rear Court" and "Linchun Joy," which for the most part praised the beauty of the consorts and ladies.

sentences.zh: 君臣酣歌，自夕達旦，以此為常。

translations.literal: Ruler and ministers sang in drunken revelry from evening until dawn, and made this their custom.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and ministers sang in drunken revelry from evening until dawn as their daily custom.

sentences.zh: 張貴妃名麗華，本兵家女，為龔貴嬪侍兒，上見而悅之，得幸，生太子深。

translations.literal: Consort Zhang, named Lihua, was originally the daughter of a military family and served as attendant to Honored Lady Gong; the emperor saw her and was pleased, gained her favor, and she bore Crown Prince Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zhang, named Lihua, was originally the daughter of a military family and served Honored Lady Gong as an attendant; the emperor saw her, was pleased, favored her, and she bore Crown Prince Shen.

sentences.zh: 貴妃發長七尺，其光可鑒，性敏慧，有神彩，進止詳華，每瞻視眄睞，光采溢目，照映左右。

translations.literal: The consort's hair was seven chi long and its luster could serve as a mirror; she was quick-witted and intelligent, with a divine brilliance; her comings and goings were measured and splendid; whenever she glanced and looked askance, radiance overflowed her eyes and shone upon those beside her.
translations.idiomatic: Her hair was seven chi long and shone like a mirror; she was quick-witted and brilliant, graceful in bearing; whenever she glanced aside, light seemed to overflow her eyes and illuminate those around her.

sentences.zh: 善候人主顏色，引薦諸宮女；

translations.literal: She was skilled at reading the sovereign's mood and recommending palace women;
translations.idiomatic: She was skilled at reading the emperor's mood and recommending palace women;

sentences.zh: 後宮鹹德之，競言其善。

translations.literal: the entire rear palace was grateful to her and vied in praising her goodness.
translations.idiomatic: the entire rear palace was grateful to her and vied in praising her virtues.

sentences.zh: 又有厭魅之術，常置淫祀於宮中，聚女巫鼓舞。

translations.literal: She also practiced arts of sorcery and curse-lifting, regularly setting up illicit sacrifices in the palace and gathering witch-women to dance and drum.
translations.idiomatic: She also practiced sorcery, regularly setting up illicit sacrifices in the palace and gathering shamanesses to dance and drum.

sentences.zh: 上怠於政事，百司啟奏，並因宦者蔡脫兒、李善度進請；

translations.literal: The emperor was negligent in government affairs; memorials from all offices were submitted through the eunuchs Cai Tuo'er and Li Shandu;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor neglected government; memorials from all offices were submitted through the eunuchs Cai Tuo'er and Li Shandu;

sentences.zh: 上倚隱囊，置張貴妃於膝上，共決之。

translations.literal: the emperor would lean on a hidden cushion, place Consort Zhang on his knees, and decide matters together with her.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor would lean on a cushioned bolster, place Consort Zhang on his knees, and decide matters with her.

sentences.zh: 李、蔡所不能記者，貴妃並為條疏，無所遺脫。

translations.literal: What Li and Cai could not remember, the consort would set out in orderly detail without omitting anything.
translations.idiomatic: What Li and Cai could not remember, the consort would set out in orderly detail without omitting anything.

sentences.zh: 因參訪外事，人間有一言一事，貴妃必先知白之；

translations.literal: Because she inquired into outside affairs, whenever there was a word or matter among the people, the consort would always learn of it first and report it;
translations.idiomatic: Because she inquired into outside affairs, whenever anything was said or done in the realm, the consort would always learn of it first and report it;

sentences.zh: 由是益加寵異，冠絕後庭。

translations.literal: thereby her favor grew ever more extraordinary, and she stood above all in the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: thereby her favor grew ever greater, and she stood above all others in the rear palace.

sentences.zh: 宦官近習，內外連結，援引宗戚，縱橫不法，賣官鬻獄，貨賂公行；

translations.literal: Eunuchs and close intimates linked inside and outside, pulling in kinsmen by marriage, acting lawlessly at will, selling offices and trading in prison sentences, bribes openly conducted;
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs and court favorites linked palace and realm, pulling in imperial kinsmen by marriage, acting lawlessly as they pleased, selling offices and trading in judicial verdicts while bribes flowed openly;

sentences.zh: 賞罰之命，不出於外。

translations.literal: Orders of reward and punishment issued from nowhere but within.
translations.idiomatic: Orders of reward and punishment came from nowhere but within the palace.

sentences.zh: 大臣有不從者，因而譖之。

translations.literal: If any high minister would not comply, they would slander him on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Any high minister who refused to go along was slandered on that account.

sentences.zh: 於是孔、張之權熏灼四方，大臣執政皆從風諂附。

translations.literal: Thus the power of Kong and Zhang scorched all four quarters; ministers in office all followed the wind and fawned.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the power of Kong Fan and Consort Zhang scorched the realm, and every minister in office followed the wind and fawned.

sentences.zh: 孔范與孔貴嬪結為兄妹；

translations.literal: Kong Fan and Consort Kong Guibin became sworn brother and sister;
translations.idiomatic: Kong Fan and Consort Kong Guibin became sworn brother and sister;

sentences.zh: 上惡聞過失，每有惡事，孔范必曲為文飾，稱揚讚美，由是寵遇優渥，言聽計從。

translations.literal: The emperor hated to hear of faults; whenever there was ill conduct, Kong Fan would invariably gloss it over and speak praise and admiration, and thereby his favored treatment was exceptionally generous—his words were heeded and plans followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hated to hear of his own faults; whenever something went wrong, Kong Fan would gloss it over and speak praise and admiration, and thereby won exceptional favor—his words were heeded and his plans followed.

sentences.zh: 群臣有諫者，輒以罪斥之。

translations.literal: Whenever any among the officials remonstrated, he would immediately have them punished and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever any official remonstrated, the emperor would immediately punish and dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人施文慶，頗涉書史，嘗事上於東宮，聰敏強記，明閒吏職，心算口占，應時條理，由是大被親幸。

translations.literal: Shi Wenqing, Attendant Drafting Secretary, had considerable learning in books and histories; he had once served the emperor when he was in the Eastern Palace. Quick-witted with a powerful memory, he was well versed in clerical duties; he could calculate in his heart and dictate orally, arranging matters promptly and in order—wherefore he came to enjoy great personal favor.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wenqing, an Attendant Drafting Secretary, was well read in history; he had served the emperor when he was crown prince. Quick-witted with a powerful memory and thoroughly versed in administrative work, he could calculate in his head and dictate answers on the spot, arranging affairs promptly and in order—wherefore he came to enjoy great personal favor.

sentences.zh: 又薦所善吳興沈客卿、陽惠朗、徐哲、暨慧景等，雲有吏能，上皆擢用之；

translations.literal: He also recommended those he favored—Shen Keqing of Wuxing, Yang Huilang, Xu Zhe, Ji Huijing, and others—saying they had administrative talent, and the emperor promoted and employed them all;
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended men he favored—Shen Keqing of Wuxing, Yang Huilang, Xu Zhe, Ji Huijing, and others—claiming they had administrative talent, and the emperor promoted and employed them all;

sentences.zh: 以客卿為中書舍人。

translations.literal: He appointed Keqing Attendant Drafting Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Shen Keqing Attendant Drafting Secretary.

sentences.zh: 客卿有口辯，頗知朝廷典故，兼掌金帛局。

translations.literal: Keqing was glib of tongue and well acquainted with court precedents, and he also supervised the Gold and Silk Office.
translations.idiomatic: Keqing was eloquent and well acquainted with court precedents, and he also supervised the Gold and Silk Office.

sentences.zh: 舊制：軍人、士人並無關市之稅。

translations.literal: Under the old regulation, soldiers and scholars paid no market toll taxes at the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old regulation, soldiers and scholars paid no market toll taxes at the passes.

sentences.zh: 上盛修宮室，窮極耳目，府庫空虛，有所興造，恆苦不給。

translations.literal: The emperor lavishly built palaces to the limit of what eye and ear could desire; the treasury was empty, and whenever he undertook construction he always suffered from insufficient funds.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lavishly built palaces to the limit of what eye and ear could desire; the treasury was empty, and whenever he undertook construction he always lacked funds.

sentences.zh: 客卿奏請，不問士庶並責關市之征，而又增重其舊。

translations.literal: Keqing memorialized requesting that without distinction of scholar or commoner, all be charged market toll taxes, and that the old rates moreover be increased.
translations.idiomatic: Keqing memorialized requesting that scholars and commoners alike be charged market toll taxes, and that the old rates be increased as well.

sentences.zh: 於是以陽惠朗為太市令，暨慧景為尚書金、倉都令史，二人家本小吏，考校簿領，纖毫不差；

translations.literal: Thereupon Yang Huilang was made Chief Market Commissioner and Ji Huijing Director of Clerks for the Ministry's Gold and Granary sections; both men came from families of petty clerks, and in auditing ledgers not the smallest item was off;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yang Huilang was made Chief Market Commissioner and Ji Huijing Director of Clerks for the Ministry's Gold and Granary sections; both came from families of petty clerks, and in auditing ledgers not the smallest item was off;

sentences.zh: 然皆不達大體，督責苛碎，聚斂無厭，士民嗟怨。

translations.literal: Yet neither understood the larger picture; their supervision was harsh and petty, their exactions insatiable, and scholars and common people groaned in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet neither understood the larger picture; their supervision was harsh and petty, their exactions insatiable, and scholars and common people groaned in resentment.

sentences.zh: 客卿總督之，每歲所入，過於常格數十倍。

translations.literal: Keqing oversaw the whole operation; each year's intake exceeded the normal quota by several tens of times.
translations.idiomatic: Keqing oversaw the whole operation; each year's intake exceeded the normal quota by several tens of times.

sentences.zh: 上大悅，益以施文慶為知人，尤見親重，小大眾事，無不委任。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and all the more regarded Shi Wenqing as one who knew men; he was especially trusted and honored, and matters great and small were none but entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and all the more regarded Shi Wenqing as a man who knew talent; he was especially trusted and honored, and matters great and small were entrusted to him without exception.

sentences.zh: 轉相汲引，珥貂蟬者五十人。

translations.literal: Through successive mutual recommendations, fifty men wore the insignia of rank at their caps.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive mutual recommendations, fifty men wore the insignia of high office at their caps.

sentences.zh: 孔范自謂文武才能，舉朝莫及，從容白上曰：「外間諸將，起自行伍，匹夫敵耳。

translations.literal: Kong Fan considered himself a man of both civil and military talent whom the whole court could not match. At his ease he told the emperor: "The generals outside all rose from the ranks—they are no match but for common soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Fan considered himself a man of both civil and military talent whom the whole court could not match. At his ease he told the emperor: "The generals outside all rose from the ranks—they are no match for anyone but common soldiers.

sentences.zh: 深見遠慮，豈其所知！」

translations.literal: Profound vision and far-reaching deliberation—how could they know such things!"
translations.idiomatic: Profound vision and far-reaching deliberation—how could they know such things!"

sentences.zh: 上以問施文慶，文慶畏范，亦以為然；

translations.literal: The emperor asked Shi Wenqing; Wenqing, in fear of Fan, also said it was so;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Shi Wenqing; Wenqing, in fear of Fan, also said it was so;

sentences.zh: 司馬申復贊之。

translations.literal: Sima Shen again endorsed it.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shen again endorsed it.

sentences.zh: 自是將帥微有過失，即奪其兵，分配文吏；

translations.literal: From this time on, whenever a commander had the slightest fault, his troops were immediately taken away and assigned to civil officials;
translations.idiomatic: From this time on, whenever a commander had the slightest fault, his troops were immediately taken away and assigned to civil officials;

sentences.zh: 奪任忠部曲以配范及蔡征。

translations.literal: Ren Zhong's personal troops were taken and assigned to Fan and Cai Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhong's personal troops were taken and assigned to Kong Fan and Cai Zheng.

sentences.zh: 由是文武解體，以至覆滅。

translations.literal: Thereby civil and military forces lost cohesion, leading ultimately to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby civil and military forces lost cohesion, leading ultimately to ruin.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，戊午朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, on the first day of the month (wuwu), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring, on the first day of the first month (wuwu), a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 2隋主命禮部尚書牛弘修五禮，勒成百卷；

translations.literal: 2 The Sui emperor ordered Niu Hong, Minister of Rites, to compile the Five Rituals, which when finished filled one hundred fascicles;
translations.idiomatic: 2 The Sui emperor ordered Niu Hong, Minister of Rites, to compile the Five Rituals, which when finished filled one hundred fascicles;

sentences.zh: 戊辰，詔行新禮。

translations.literal: On wuchen, an edict ordered the new rituals put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen an edict ordered the new rituals put into practice.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊午，隋以尚書左僕射高熲為左領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: In the third month, on wuwu, Sui appointed Gao Jiong, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, as Left General Who Leads the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuwu, Sui appointed Gao Jiong, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, as Left General Who Leads the Army.

sentences.zh: 3豐州刺史章大寶，昭達之子也，在州貪縱，朝廷以太僕卿李暈代之。

translations.literal: 3 Zhang Dabao, governor of Feng Province, was the son of Zhang Zhaoda; greedy and licentious in his province, the court sent Li Hun, Grand Stable Master, to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: 3 Zhang Dabao, governor of Feng Province and son of Zhang Zhaoda, was greedy and licentious in his province; the court sent Li Hun, Grand Stable Master, to replace him.

sentences.zh: 暈將至，辛酉，大寶襲殺暈，舉兵反。

translations.literal: As Hun was about to arrive, on xinyou Dabao launched a surprise attack and killed Hun, then raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: As Hun was about to arrive, on xinyou Dabao launched a surprise attack and killed Hun, then raised troops in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 4隋大司徒郢公王誼與隋主有舊，其子尚帝女蘭陵公主。

translations.literal: 4 Wang Yi, Duke of Ying and Grand Minister of Education in Sui, had old ties with the Sui emperor; his son had married the emperor's daughter, Princess Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: 4 Wang Yi, Duke of Ying and Grand Minister of Education in Sui, had old ties with the Sui emperor; his son had married the emperor's daughter, Princess Lanling.

sentences.zh: 帝待之恩禮稍薄，誼頗怨望。

translations.literal: The emperor's gracious treatment grew somewhat thin, and Yi nursed considerable resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's gracious treatment grew somewhat thin, and Yi nursed considerable resentment.

sentences.zh: 或告誼自言名應圖讖，相表當王；

translations.literal: Someone reported that Yi had said his name matched omens in prognostic texts and that his physiognomy showed he was destined to be king;
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Yi had said his name matched omens in prognostic texts and that his physiognomy showed he was destined to be king;

sentences.zh: 公卿奏誼大逆不道。

translations.literal: The highest officials memorialized that Yi had committed treason.
translations.idiomatic: The highest officials memorialized that Yi had committed treason.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，賜誼死。

translations.literal: On renyin, Yi was sentenced to death by imperial grant.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Yi was sentenced to death by imperial grant.

sentences.zh: 戊申，隋主還長安。

translations.literal: On wushen, the Sui emperor returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the Sui emperor returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 5章大寶遣其將楊通攻建安，不克。

translations.literal: 5 Zhang Dabao sent his general Yang Tong to attack Jian'an without success.
translations.idiomatic: 5 Zhang Dabao sent his general Yang Tong to attack Jian'an without success.

sentences.zh: 官軍將至，大寶眾潰，逃入山，為追兵所擒，夷三族。

translations.literal: As government troops were arriving, Dabao's forces broke up; he fled into the mountains, was captured by pursuers, and his three clans were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: As government troops were arriving, Dabao's forces broke up; he fled into the mountains, was captured by pursuers, and his three clans were exterminated.

sentences.zh: 6隋度支尚書長孫平奏，「令民間每秋家出粟麥一石已下，貧富為差，儲之當社，委社司檢校，以備凶年，名曰義倉。」

translations.literal: 6 Changsun Ping, Director of the Revenue Ministry in Sui, memorialized: "Let each household in autumn contribute grain and wheat below one picul according to the measure of rich and poor; store it at the local altar, entrust inspection to the altar officers, and reserve it against famine years—this shall be called the Charity Granary."
translations.idiomatic: 6 Changsun Ping, Director of the Revenue Ministry in Sui, memorialized: "Let each household in autumn contribute grain and wheat below one picul according to the measure of rich and poor; store it at the local altar, entrust inspection to the altar officers, and reserve it against famine years—this shall be called the Charity Granary."

sentences.zh: 隋主從之。

translations.literal: The Sui emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 五月，甲申，初詔郡、縣置義倉。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jiashen, an edict first ordered counties and commanderies to establish Charity Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jiashen an edict first ordered counties and commanderies to establish Charity Granaries.

sentences.zh: 平，儉之子也。

translations.literal: Ping was the son of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Ping was the son of Jian.

sentences.zh: 時民間多妄稱老、小以免賦役，山東承北齊之弊政，戶口租調，奸偽尤多。

translations.literal: At that time many among the people falsely claimed to be old or young to evade tax and corvée; Shandong, inheriting the corrupt policies of Northern Qi, had especially many frauds in household registration and land tax.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many among the people falsely claimed to be old or young to evade tax and corvée; Shandong, inheriting the corrupt policies of Northern Qi, had especially many frauds in household registration and land tax.

sentences.zh: 隋主命州縣大索貌閱，戶口不實者，裡正、黨長遠配；

translations.literal: The Sui emperor ordered the provinces and counties to conduct a thorough household inspection and face verification; where registrations were false, the neighborhood heads and clan chiefs were exiled to distant posts;
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor ordered the provinces and counties to conduct a thorough household inspection and face verification; where registrations were false, the neighborhood heads and clan chiefs were exiled to distant posts;

sentences.zh: 大功以下，皆令析籍，以防容隱。

translations.literal: All relatives within the degree of dagong mourning and below were ordered to separate their household registers to prevent concealment.
translations.idiomatic: All relatives within the degree of dagong mourning and below were ordered to separate their household registers to prevent concealment.

sentences.zh: 於是計帳得新附一百六十四萬餘口。

translations.literal: Thereupon the census accounts showed more than 1.64 million newly registered persons.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the census accounts showed more than 1.64 million newly registered persons.

sentences.zh: 高熲又言民間課輸無定簿，難以推校，請為輸籍法，遍下諸州，帝從之，自是奸無所容矣。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong further said that among the people tax payments had no fixed register and were hard to verify; he requested that a Delivery Register Law be instituted and sent to all provinces. The emperor agreed, and from then on fraud had nowhere to hide.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong further said that among the people tax payments had no fixed register and were hard to verify; he requested that a Delivery Register Law be instituted and sent to all provinces. The emperor agreed, and from then on fraud had nowhere to hide.

sentences.zh: 諸州調物，每歲河南自潼關，河北自蒲板，輸長安者相屬於路，晝夜不絕者數月。

translations.literal: Each year tribute goods from the provinces—from Tong Pass in Henan and from Puban in Hebei—those bound for Chang'an followed one after another along the roads without ceasing day or night for months.
translations.idiomatic: Each year tribute goods from the provinces—from Tong Pass in Henan and from Puban in Hebei—those bound for Chang'an followed one after another along the roads without ceasing day or night for months.

sentences.zh: 7梁主殂，謚曰孝明皇帝，廟號世宗，世宗孝慈儉約，境內安之。

translations.literal: 7 The Liang ruler died; his posthumous title was Emperor Xiaoming, temple name Shizong. Shizong was filial, benevolent, and frugal, and the realm within his borders was at peace.
translations.idiomatic: 7 The Liang ruler died; his posthumous title was Emperor Xiaoming, temple name Shizong. Shizong was filial, benevolent, and frugal, and the realm within his borders was at peace.

sentences.zh: 太子琮嗣位。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Cong succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Cong succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 8初，突厥阿波可汗既與沙缽略有隙，分而為二，阿波浸強，東距都斤，西越金山，龜茲、鐵勒、伊吾及西域諸胡悉附之，號西突厥。

translations.literal: 8 Earlier, the Türk qaghan Abo, having had a rupture with Shebolue, had split into two; Abo gradually grew strong, holding the region east to Dujin and west beyond Jinshan Mountain; Kucha, the Tiele, Yiwu, and all the Hu of the Western Regions attached to him, and he was called the Western Türks.
translations.idiomatic: 8 Earlier, the Türk qaghan Abo, having had a rupture with Shebolue, had split into two; Abo gradually grew strong, holding the region east to Dujin and west beyond Jinshan Mountain; Kucha, the Tiele, Yiwu, and all the Hu of the Western Regions attached to him, and he was called the Western Türks.

sentences.zh: 隋主亦遣上大將軍元契使於阿波以撫之。

translations.literal: The Sui emperor also dispatched Senior General Yuan Qi as envoy to Abo to mollify him.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor also dispatched Senior General Yuan Qi as envoy to Abo to mollify him.

sentences.zh: 9秋，七月，庚申，遣散騎常侍王話等聘於隋。

translations.literal: 9 In autumn, the seventh month, on gengshen, he dispatched Attendant Cavalier Wang Hua and others on a mission of courtesy to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: 9 In autumn, the seventh month, on gengshen, the Chen emperor dispatched Attendant Cavalier Wang Hua and others on a mission of courtesy to Sui.

sentences.zh: 突厥沙缽略既為達頭所困，又畏契丹，遣使告急於隋，請將部落度漠南，寄居白道川。

translations.literal: The Türk Shebolue, having been beset by Datou and also fearing the Khitan, sent envoys to Sui in urgent appeal, asking to lead his tribes south across the desert and lodge at White Road River.
translations.idiomatic: The Türk Shebolue, having been beset by Datou and also fearing the Khitan, sent envoys to Sui in urgent appeal, asking to lead his tribes south across the desert and lodge at White Road River.

sentences.zh: 隋主許之，命晉王廣以兵援之，給以衣食，賜之車服鼓吹。

translations.literal: The Sui emperor granted this, ordered Prince of Jin Guang to assist him with troops, supplied food and clothing, and bestowed chariots, robes, and musical escort.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor granted this, ordered Prince of Jin Yang Guang to assist him with troops, supplied food and clothing, and bestowed chariots, robes, and musical escort.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略因西擊阿波，破之。

translations.literal: Shebolue thereupon struck west against Abo and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Shebolue thereupon struck west against Abo and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 而阿拔國乘虛掠其妻子；

translations.literal: But Abo's people seized the opportunity to plunder his wife and children;
translations.idiomatic: But Abo's people seized the opportunity to plunder his wife and children;

sentences.zh: 官軍為擊阿拔，敗之，所獲悉與沙缽略。

translations.literal: Government troops attacked the Abo forces, defeated them, and gave all the captives to Shebolue.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops attacked Abo's forces, defeated them, and gave all the captives to Shebolue.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略大喜，乃立約，以磧為界，因上表曰：「天無二日，土無二王。

translations.literal: Shebolue was greatly pleased, then established a treaty with the desert as boundary, and submitted a memorial saying: "Heaven has not two suns; earth has not two kings.
translations.idiomatic: Shebolue was greatly pleased, then established a treaty with the desert as boundary, and submitted a memorial saying: "Heaven has not two suns; earth has not two kings.

sentences.zh: 大隋皇帝，真皇帝也！

translations.literal: The Great Sui emperor is the true emperor!
translations.idiomatic: The Great Sui emperor is the true emperor!

sentences.zh: 豈敢阻兵恃險，偷竊名號！

translations.literal: How would I dare to rely on arms, hold to defensible terrain, and steal a title!
translations.idiomatic: How would I dare to rely on arms, hold to defensible terrain, and steal a title!

sentences.zh: 今感慕淳風，歸心有道，屈膝稽顙，永為籓附。」

translations.literal: Now moved by your pure culture, my heart turns to the Way; kneeling and bowing my forehead to the ground, I shall forever be your vassal ally."
translations.idiomatic: Now moved by your pure culture, my heart turns to the Way; kneeling and bowing my forehead to the ground, I shall forever be your vassal ally."

sentences.zh: 遣其子庫合真入朝。

translations.literal: He sent his son Kuhezhan to court.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his son Kuhezhan to court.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙戌，庫合真至長安。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on bingxu, Kuhezhan arrived at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on bingxu, Kuhezhan arrived at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 隋主下詔曰：「沙缽略往雖與和，猶是二國；

translations.literal: The Sui emperor issued an edict: "Shebolue, though formerly at peace, was still a second state;
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor issued an edict: "Shebolue, though formerly at peace, was still a second state;

sentences.zh: 今作君臣，便成一體。」

translations.literal: now as ruler and subject, we have become one body."
translations.idiomatic: now as ruler and subject, we have become one body."

sentences.zh: 因命肅告郊廟，普頒遠近；

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered solemn announcement at the suburban altars and temples, promulgated far and near;
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon ordered solemn announcement at the suburban altars and temples, promulgated far and near;

sentences.zh: 凡賜沙缽略詔，不稱其名。

translations.literal: In all edicts granted to Shebolue, his personal name was not used.
translations.idiomatic: In all edicts granted to Shebolue, his personal name was not used.

sentences.zh: 宴庫合真於內殿，引見皇后，賞勞甚厚。

translations.literal: He feasted Kuhezhan in the inner hall, presented him to the empress, and rewarded him with great generosity.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted Kuhezhan in the inner hall, presented him to the empress, and rewarded him with great generosity.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略大悅，自是歲時貢獻不絕。

translations.literal: Shebolue was greatly pleased; from then on tribute and offerings never ceased season by season.
translations.idiomatic: Shebolue was greatly pleased; from then on tribute and offerings never ceased season by season.

sentences.zh: 10九月，將軍湛文徹侵隋和州，隋儀同三司費寶首擊擒之。

translations.literal: 10 In the ninth month, General Zhan Wenche invaded Sui's He Province; Fei Baoshou, Sui official of third rank ceremonial parity, attacked and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: 10 In the ninth month, General Zhan Wenche invaded Sui's He Province; Fei Baoshou, a Sui official of third rank ceremonial parity, attacked and captured him.

sentences.zh: 丙子，隋使李若等來聘。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Sui envoys Li Ruo and others came on a mission of courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Sui envoys Li Ruo and others came on a mission of courtesy.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬辰，隋以上柱國楊素為信州總管。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on renchen, Sui appointed Senior Pillar of State Yang Su as Overall Commander of Xin Province.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on renchen, Sui appointed Senior Pillar of State Yang Su as Overall Commander of Xin Province.

sentences.zh: 11初，北地傅縡以庶子事上於東宮，及即位，遷秘書監、右衛將軍兼中書通事舍人，負才使氣，人多怨之。

translations.literal: 11 Earlier, Fu Xiu of Beidi had served the emperor as tutor when he was in the Eastern Palace; when the emperor ascended the throne, he was promoted to Director of the Secretariat, Right Guard General, and concurrently Attendant Drafting Secretary for General Affairs—talented but overbearing, and many resented him.
translations.idiomatic: 11 Earlier, Fu Xiu of Beidi had served the emperor as tutor when he was crown prince; when the emperor ascended the throne, he was promoted to Director of the Secretariat, Right Guard General, and concurrently Attendant Drafting Secretary for General Affairs—talented but overbearing, and many resented him.

sentences.zh: 施文慶、沈客卿共譖縡受高麗使金，上收縡下獄。

translations.literal: Shi Wenqing and Shen Keqing together slandered Xiu for accepting gold from a Goguryeo envoy; the emperor had Xiu arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wenqing and Shen Keqing together slandered Fu Xiu for accepting gold from a Goguryeo envoy; the emperor had Xiu arrested and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 縡於獄中上書曰：「夫君人者，恭事上帝，子愛下民，省嗜欲，遠諂佞，未明求夜，日旰忘食，是以澤被區宇，慶流子孫。

translations.literal: From prison Xiu submitted a memorial saying: "A ruler should reverently serve Heaven, love the people as his children, restrain appetites, keep flatterers at a distance, seek understanding before dawn and forget to eat until dusk—thereby his grace covers the realm and blessing flows to his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: From prison Fu Xiu submitted a memorial saying: "A ruler should reverently serve Heaven, love the people as his children, restrain appetites, keep flatterers at a distance, seek understanding before dawn and forget to eat until dusk—thereby his grace covers the realm and blessing flows to his descendants.

sentences.zh: 陛下頃來酒色過度，不虔郊廟大神，專媚淫昏之鬼，小人在側，宦豎弄權。

translations.literal: Your Majesty of late has indulged excessively in wine and women, is not reverent toward the gods of the suburban altars and grand temples, and dotes exclusively on lewd and deluded spirits; petty men stand at your side and eunuchs manipulate power.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty of late has indulged excessively in wine and women, is not reverent toward the gods of the suburban altars and grand temples, and dotes exclusively on lewd and deluded spirits; petty men stand at your side and eunuchs manipulate power.

sentences.zh: 惡忠直若仇讎，視生民如草芥。

translations.literal: You hate the loyal and upright as though they were mortal enemies and regard the living people as mere grass and chaff.
translations.idiomatic: You hate the loyal and upright as though they were mortal enemies and regard the living people as mere grass and chaff.

sentences.zh: 後宮曳綺繡，廄馬餘菽粟，百姓流離，殭屍蔽野，貨賄公行，帑藏損耗。

translations.literal: In the rear palace silks and brocades trail behind; in the stables horses have surplus beans and grain; the common people wander homeless; unburied corpses cover the fields; bribes are openly traded; the treasury is depleted.
translations.idiomatic: In the rear palace silks and brocades trail behind; in the stables horses have surplus beans and grain; the common people wander homeless; unburied corpses cover the fields; bribes are openly traded; the treasury is depleted.

sentences.zh: 神怒民怨，眾叛親離，臣恐東南王氣自斯而盡。」

translations.literal: The gods are angry and the people resentful; all abandon you and kinsmen depart—I fear the kingly qi of the southeast ends here."
translations.idiomatic: The gods are angry and the people resentful; all abandon you and kinsmen depart—I fear the kingly qi of the southeast ends here."

sentences.zh: 書奏，上大怒。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor was greatly enraged.

sentences.zh: 頃之，意稍解，遣使謂縡曰：「我欲赦卿，卿能改過不？」

translations.literal: Before long his anger somewhat eased; he sent an envoy to tell Xiu: "I wish to pardon you—can you reform your ways?"
translations.idiomatic: Before long his anger somewhat eased; he sent an envoy to tell Fu Xiu: "I wish to pardon you—can you reform your ways?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣心如面，臣面可改，則臣心可改。」

translations.literal: Xiu replied: "Your servant's heart is like my face—if my face could be changed, then my heart could be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Xiu replied: "Your servant's heart is like my face—if my face could be changed, then my heart could be changed."

sentences.zh: 上益怒，令宦者李善慶窮治其事，遂賜死獄中。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still more angry, ordered the eunuch Li Shanqing to investigate the matter thoroughly, and ultimately had him granted death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew still more angry, ordered the eunuch Li Shanqing to investigate the matter thoroughly, and ultimately had him granted death in prison.

sentences.zh: 上每當郊祀，常稱疾不行，故縡言及之。

translations.literal: Whenever the time came for suburban sacrifice, the emperor would usually claim illness and not go—therefore Xiu had spoken of it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the time came for suburban sacrifice, the emperor would usually claim illness and not go—therefore Fu Xiu had spoken of it.

sentences.zh: 是歲，梁大將軍戚昕以舟師襲公安，不克而還。

translations.literal: That year, General Qi Xin of Liang led a fleet in a surprise attack on Gong'an without success and returned.
translations.idiomatic: That year, General Qi Xin of Liang led a fleet in a surprise attack on Gong'an without success and returned.

sentences.zh: 12隋主征梁主叔父太尉吳王岑入朝，拜大將軍，封懷義公，因留不遣；

translations.literal: 12 The Sui emperor summoned the Liang ruler's uncle, Grand Preceptor and Prince of Wu Chen, to court, appointed him Grand General and enfeoffed him as Duke of Huaiyi, then detained him and did not send him back;
translations.idiomatic: 12 The Sui emperor summoned the Liang ruler's uncle, Grand Preceptor and Prince of Wu Chen, to court, appointed him Grand General and enfeoffed him as Duke of Huaiyi, then detained him and did not send him back;

sentences.zh: 復置江陵總管以監之。

translations.literal: He reestablished the Jiangling overall command to oversee affairs there.
translations.idiomatic: He reestablished the Jiangling overall command to oversee affairs there.

sentences.zh: 梁大將軍許世武密以城召荊州刺史宜黃侯慧紀；

translations.literal: General Xu Shiwu of Liang secretly offered the city to summon Jing Province governor Marquis of Yihuang Hui Ji;
translations.idiomatic: General Xu Shiwu of Liang secretly offered the city to summon Jing Province governor Marquis of Yihuang Hui Ji;

sentences.zh: 謀洩，梁主殺之。

translations.literal: When the plot leaked out, the Liang ruler had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot leaked out, the Liang ruler had him killed.

sentences.zh: 慧紀，高祖之從孫也。

translations.literal: Hui Ji was a grandnephew of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Hui Ji was a grandnephew of Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 13隋主使司農少卿崔仲方發丁三萬，於朔方、靈武築長城，東距河，西至綏州，綿歷七百里，以遏胡寇。

translations.literal: 13 The Sui emperor had Vice Minister of Agriculture Cui Zhongfang conscript thirty thousand laborers to build the Long Wall at Shuofang and Lingwu, from the river in the east to Suizhou in the west, running seven hundred li in all, to block Hu raiders.
translations.idiomatic: 13 The Sui emperor had Vice Minister of Agriculture Cui Zhongfang conscript thirty thousand laborers to build the Long Wall at Shuofang and Lingwu, from the river in the east to Suizhou in the west, running seven hundred li in all, to block Hu raiders.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，梁改元廣運。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, Liang changed the era name to Guangyun.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring, the first month, Liang changed the era name to Guangyun.

sentences.zh: 2甲子，党項羌請降於隋。

translations.literal: 2 On jiazi, the Di and Qiang of Dang sought surrender to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: 2 On jiazi the Di and Qiang of Dang sought surrender to Sui.

sentences.zh: 庚午，隋頒歷於突厥。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Sui issued its calendar to the Türks.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Sui issued its calendar to the Türks.

sentences.zh: 二月，隋始令刺史上佐每歲暮更入朝，上考課。

translations.literal: In the second month, Sui for the first time ordered that each year-end the senior assistants of provincial governors should rotate to court for annual assessment.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Sui for the first time ordered that each year-end the senior assistants of provincial governors should rotate to court for annual assessment.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，隋復令崔仲方發丁十五萬，於朔方以東，緣邊險要，築數十城。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Sui again ordered Cui Zhongfang to conscript one hundred fifty thousand laborers east of Shuofang, along strategic points on the border, to build several tens of forts.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Sui again ordered Cui Zhongfang to conscript one hundred fifty thousand laborers east of Shuofang, along strategic points on the border, to build several tens of forts.

sentences.zh: 3丙申，立皇弟叔謨為巴東王，叔顯為臨江王，叔坦為新會王，叔隆為新寧王。

translations.literal: 3 On the day bingshen, the emperor's younger brother Shu Mo was installed as Prince of Badong, Shu Xian as Prince of Linjiang, Shu Tan as Prince of Xinhui, and Shu Long as Prince of Xinning.
translations.idiomatic: 3 On bingshen day the emperor's younger brothers were ennobled: Shu Mo as Prince of Badong, Shu Xian as Prince of Linjiang, Shu Tan as Prince of Xinhui, and Shu Long as Prince of Xinning.

sentences.zh: 4庚子，隋大赦。

translations.literal: 4 On the day gengzi, Sui proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: 4 On gengzi day Sui issued a general pardon.

sentences.zh: 三月，己未，洛陽男子高德上書，請隋主為太上皇，傳位皇太子。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day jiwei, a man of Luoyang named Gao De submitted a memorial asking that the Sui emperor become Retired Emperor and transfer the throne to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month on jiwei, a Luoyang commoner named Gao De submitted a memorial urging the Sui emperor to abdicate in favor of his crown prince and take the title of Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕承天命，撫育蒼生，日旰孜孜，猶恐不逮。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have received Heaven's mandate and nurture the people; from dawn till dusk I toil diligently, yet still fear I fall short.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Heaven's mandate rests upon me; I labor from dawn till dusk to nurture the people, and still fear I am not equal to the task.

sentences.zh: 豈效近代帝王，傳位於子，自求逸樂者哉！

translations.literal: How could I imitate the rulers of recent times who transfer the throne to their sons and seek ease and pleasure for themselves!
translations.idiomatic: Why should I imitate recent emperors who abdicate for their sons and retire to idleness and pleasure!

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己亥，遣周磻等聘於隋。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day jihai, Zhou Pan and others were sent on a mission of friendship to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month on jihai, Zhou Pan and others were dispatched on a diplomatic mission to Sui.

sentences.zh: 5五月，丁巳，立皇子莊為會稽王。

translations.literal: 5 In the fifth month, on the day dingsi, the emperor's son Zhuang was installed as Prince of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: 5 In the fifth month on dingsi the emperor's son Zhuang was made Prince of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 6秋，八月，隋遣散騎常侍裴豪等來聘。

translations.literal: 6 In autumn, the eighth month, Sui dispatched the Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Pei Hao and others on a mission of friendship.
translations.idiomatic: 6 In autumn, the eighth month, Sui sent Pei Hao, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and others on a friendly visit.

sentences.zh: 戊申，隋申明公李穆卒，葬以殊禮。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, Li Mu, Duke of Shenming of Sui, died and was buried with special honors.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day Li Mu, Duke of Shenming, died and was buried with extraordinary rites.

sentences.zh: 閏月，丁卯，隋太子勇鎮洛陽。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the day dingmao, the Sui Crown Prince Yong was stationed at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month on dingmao, Crown Prince Yong of Sui took up residence at Luoyang as governor.

sentences.zh: 隋上柱國郕公梁士彥討尉遲迥，所當必破，代迥為相州刺史。

translations.literal: Liang Shiyan, Duke of Cheng and Grand General of Sui, campaigning against Yu Chi Jiong, broke every force he met and replaced Jiong as governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shiyan, Duke of Cheng and a grand general of Sui, in campaigning against Yuchi Jiong shattered every force in his path and took Jiong's place as governor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 隋主忌之，召還長安。

translations.literal: The Sui emperor was jealous of him and summoned him back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor grew wary of him and recalled him to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 上柱國杞公宇文忻與隋主少相厚，善用兵，有威名。

translations.literal: Yuwen Xin, Duke of Qi and Grand General, had been close to the Sui emperor since youth; he was skilled in warfare and enjoyed a fearsome reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Xin, Duke of Qi and a grand general, had been on intimate terms with the Sui emperor since youth; he was a gifted commander with a formidable reputation.

sentences.zh: 隋主亦忌之，以譴去官。

translations.literal: The Sui emperor was also jealous of him and removed him from office on pretext of censure.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor likewise grew wary and dismissed him from office under a reprimand.

sentences.zh: 與柱國舒公劉昉皆被疏遠，閒居無事，頗懷怨望，數相往來，陰謀不軌。

translations.literal: He and Liu Fang, Duke of Shu and a pillar of state, were both kept at a distance; idle at home with nothing to do, they nursed considerable resentment, visited each other repeatedly, and plotted rebellion in secret.
translations.idiomatic: He and Liu Fang, Duke of Shu, were both sidelined; idle and embittered, they met frequently and conspired in secret.

sentences.zh: 忻欲使士彥於蒲州起兵，己為內應，士彥之甥裴通預其謀而告之。

translations.literal: Xin wished Shiyan to raise troops at Pu Province while he himself served as an inside collaborator; Pei Tong, Shiyan's nephew, took part in the plot and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Xin planned for Shiyan to raise an army at Pu Province while he acted as an inside accomplice; Shiyan's nephew Pei Tong learned of the plot and informed the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝隱其事，以士彥為晉州刺史，欲觀其意；

translations.literal: The emperor concealed the matter, appointed Shiyan governor of Jin Province, and wished to observe his intent;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept the report secret, appointed Shiyan governor of Jin Province, and watched to see what he would do;

sentences.zh: 士彥忻然，謂昉等曰：「天也！」

translations.literal: Shiyan was delighted and said to Fang and the others: "Heaven's doing!"
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan was overjoyed and told Fang and the others, "This is Heaven's work!"

sentences.zh: 又請儀同三司薛摩兒為長史，帝亦許之。

translations.literal: He also requested Xue Mo'er, third-rank ceremonial peer, as his chief administrator, and the emperor also granted it.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that Xue Mo'er, a third-rank ceremonial peer, serve as his chief administrator, and the emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 後與公卿朝謁，帝令左右執士彥、忻、昉等於行間。

translations.literal: Later, during an audience with the officials, the emperor ordered his attendants to seize Shiyan, Xin, Fang, and the others in the procession.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at an audience with the court, the emperor had his attendants seize Shiyan, Xin, Fang, and the rest in mid-procession.

sentences.zh: 詰之，初猶不伏。

translations.literal: He interrogated them; at first they still would not confess.
translations.idiomatic: Under interrogation they at first refused to admit guilt.

sentences.zh: 捕薛摩兒適至，命之庭對，摩兒具論始末，士彥失色，顧謂摩兒曰：「汝殺我！」

translations.literal: Xue Mo'er, who had been arrested, happened to arrive; the emperor ordered a confrontation in court, and Mo'er set forth the whole affair in detail; Shiyan lost color and turned to Mo'er, saying: "You have killed me!"
translations.idiomatic: Xue Mo'er was brought in just then; ordered to testify before the court, he related the plot in full. Shiyan turned pale and cried to Mo'er, "You have destroyed me!"

sentences.zh: 丙子，士彥、忻、昉皆伏誅，叔侄、兄弟免死除名。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, Shiyan, Xin, and Fang were all executed; their uncles, nephews, and brothers were spared death but struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day Shiyan, Xin, and Fang were all put to death; their uncles, nephews, and brothers were spared but stripped of rank and name.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛巳，隋主素服臨射殿，命百官射三家資物以為誡。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day xinsi, the Sui emperor in plain garb attended the Archery Hall and ordered the officials to shoot at the possessions of the three clans as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month on xinsi the Sui emperor, dressed in mourning white, appeared at the Archery Hall and had officials shoot at the family goods of the three conspirators' houses as a cautionary lesson.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己酉，隋以兵部尚書楊尚希為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jiyou, Sui made Yang Shangxi, Minister of War, Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month on jiyou, Sui transferred Yang Shangxi from Minister of War to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 隋主每旦臨朝，日昃不倦，尚希諫曰：「周文王以憂勤損壽，武王以安樂延年。

translations.literal: The Sui emperor attended court every morning and did not weary even when the sun slanted westward; Shangxi remonstrated, saying: "King Wen of Zhou shortened his life through worry and diligence; King Wu extended his years through ease and contentment.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor held court each dawn and worked past sundown without tiring; Shangxi advised him: "King Wen of Zhou wore himself out with ceaseless cares and died young; King Wu lived long by trusting others to govern.

sentences.zh: 願陛下舉大綱，責成宰輔。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would take hold of the great framework and hold the chief ministers accountable for results.
translations.idiomatic: Let Your Majesty grasp the broad outlines of policy and hold your ministers responsible for execution.

sentences.zh: 繁碎之務，非人主所宜親也。」

translations.literal: Trivial and minute affairs are not what a ruler should attend to in person."
translations.idiomatic: Petty administrative details are not work for the Son of Heaven himself."

sentences.zh: 帝善之而不能從。

translations.literal: The emperor approved but could not follow the advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the counsel but could not bring himself to follow it.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，隋置山南道行台於襄州；

translations.literal: On the day guichou, Sui established the Shannan Circuit Executive Office at Xiang Province;
translations.idiomatic: On guichou day Sui established a circuit executive office for Shannan at Xiangzhou;

sentences.zh: 以秦王俊為尚書令。

translations.literal: Qin Wang Jun was made Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Wang Jun was appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 俊妃崔氏生男，隋主喜，頒賜群官。

translations.literal: Jun's consort, the Lady Cui, bore a son; the Sui emperor rejoiced and distributed rewards to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun's consort Lady Cui gave birth to a son, the delighted Sui emperor showered gifts on the entire bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 直秘書內省博陵李文博，家素貧，人往賀之，文博曰：「賞罰之設，功過所存。

translations.literal: Li Wenbo of Boling, a clerk in the Secretariat, had always been poor; when people came to congratulate him, Wenbo said: "Rewards and punishments are established to mark merit and fault.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wenbo of Boling, a clerk in the Secretariat, had always been poor; when visitors came to congratulate him on the imperial largesse, Wenbo said: "Rewards and punishments exist to honor merit and penalize fault.

sentences.zh: 今王妃生男，於群官何事，乃妄受賞也！」

translations.literal: Now that the prince's consort has borne a son, what does that matter to the officials, that we should accept rewards unworthily!"
translations.idiomatic: The prince's consort bore a son — what has that to do with us officials that we should accept a reward we did not earn!"

sentences.zh: 聞者愧之。

translations.literal: Those who heard were ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard were put to shame.

sentences.zh: 7癸亥，以尚書僕射江總為尚書令，吏部尚書謝胄為僕射。

translations.literal: 7 On the day guihai, Jiang Zong, Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was made Director; Xie Zhou, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, was made Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: 7 On guihai day Jiang Zong was promoted from Vice Director to Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Xie Zhou, Minister of Personnel, became Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己卯，大赦。
