translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day jimao, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month on jimao a general pardon was issued.

sentences.zh: 8吐谷渾可汗誇呂在位百年，屢因喜怒廢殺太子。

translations.literal: 8 Kualü, khan of the Tuyuhun, had reigned for a hundred years and repeatedly deposed and killed crown princes in fits of anger or pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: 8 Kualü, khan of the Tuyuhun, had ruled a hundred years and repeatedly deposed and killed heirs apparent on whim.

sentences.zh: 後太子懼，謀執誇呂而降；

translations.literal: Later a crown prince, in fear, plotted to seize Kualü and surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Eventually a crown prince, fearing for his life, plotted to seize Kualü and defect;

sentences.zh: 請兵於隋邊吏，秦州總管河間王弘請以兵應之，隋主不許。

translations.literal: he requested troops from a Sui border official; Hong, Prince of Hejian and overall commander of Qin Province, asked to respond with troops, but the Sui emperor would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: he asked Sui border officials for military support; Hong, Prince of Hejian and commander of Qin Province, offered to send troops, but the Sui emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 太子謀洩，為誇呂所殺，復立其少子嵬王訶為太子。

translations.literal: The crown prince's plot leaked out and he was killed by Kualü, who again installed his youngest son, Prince Wei He, as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was discovered; Kualü executed the prince and installed his youngest son, Prince Wei He, as the new heir.

sentences.zh: 疊州刺史杜粲請因其釁而討之，隋主又不許。

translations.literal: Du Can, governor of Die Province, asked to attack them while they were embroiled in strife, but the Sui emperor again would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Du Can, governor of Die Province, urged an attack while they were in turmoil, but again the Sui emperor declined.

sentences.zh: 是歲，嵬王訶復懼誅，謀帥部落萬五千戶降隋，遣使詣闕，請兵迎之。

translations.literal: That year Prince Wei He again feared execution and planned to lead fifteen thousand households of his tribe in submission to Sui; he sent envoys to the capital to request troops to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: That year Prince Wei He again feared death and planned to lead fifteen thousand tribal households in surrender to Sui, dispatching envoys to the capital to ask for troops to escort them in.

sentences.zh: 隋主曰：「渾賊風俗，特異人倫，父既不慈，子復不孝。

translations.literal: The Sui emperor said: "The customs of these Hun bandits are utterly unlike human propriety; the father is not loving, and the son is not filial.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor said: "These Tuyuhun barbarians follow customs alien to human decency — the father unloving, the son unfilial.

sentences.zh: 朕以德訓人，何有成其惡逆乎！」

translations.literal: I instruct people with virtue — why should I abet their wicked rebellion!"
translations.idiomatic: I govern by moral example — why should I encourage their treachery!"

sentences.zh: 乃謂使者曰：「父有過失，子當諫爭，豈可潛謀非法，受不孝之名！

translations.literal: He then told the envoys: "When a father has faults, a son should remonstrate openly — how can one plot in secret unlawful acts and incur the name of unfiliality!
translations.idiomatic: Then he told the envoys: "When a father errs, a son should remonstrate openly — not plot treason in secret and bear the stain of unfiliality!

sentences.zh: 溥天之下，皆朕臣妾，各為善事，即稱朕心。

translations.literal: All beneath broad Heaven are my subjects; if each does good deeds, that will accord with my heart.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven are my subjects; let each do what is right, and that will satisfy me.

sentences.zh: 嵬王既欲歸朕，唯教嵬王為臣子之法，不可遠遣兵馬，助為惡事！」

translations.literal: Since Prince Wei wishes to submit to me, I need only teach him the way of a subject and minister — I cannot dispatch troops from afar to help him do evil!"
translations.idiomatic: If Prince Wei truly wishes to submit, I need only instruct him in the duties of a loyal subject — I will not dispatch an army to abet his crime!"

sentences.zh: 嵬王訶乃止。

translations.literal: Prince Wei He then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei He abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，戊寅，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, on the day wuyin, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring, the first month on wuyin a general amnesty was issued and a new reign era was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 2癸巳，隋主享太廟。

translations.literal: 2 On the day guisi, the Sui emperor offered sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: 2 On guisi day the Sui emperor performed rites at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 乙未，隋制諸州歲貢士三人。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, Sui instituted the rule that each province should annually recommend three scholars.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day Sui decreed that each province should send three recommended scholars annually.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁巳，隋主朝日於東郊。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day dingsi, the Sui emperor worshipped the sun at the Eastern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month on dingsi the Sui emperor performed the solar rite at the Eastern Suburb.

sentences.zh: 遣兼散騎常侍王亨等聘於隋。

translations.literal: Wang Heng, concurrent Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and others were sent on a mission of friendship to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Heng, concurrent Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and others were dispatched on a diplomatic mission to Sui.

sentences.zh: 隋發丁男十萬餘人修長城，二旬而罷。

translations.literal: Sui mobilized more than a hundred thousand conscript laborers to repair the Great Wall; the work was halted after twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: Sui conscripted more than a hundred thousand men to repair the Great Wall, stopping after twenty days.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，於揚州開山陽瀆以通運。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the Shanyang Canal was opened at Yang Province to facilitate transport.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, the Shanyang Canal was dug at Yangzhou to open a transport route.

sentences.zh: 3突厥沙缽略可汗遣其子入貢於隋，因請獵於恆、代之間，隋主許之，仍遣人賜以酒食。

translations.literal: 3 Shabolu, khan of the Turks, sent his son to offer tribute to Sui and meanwhile requested to hunt between Heng and Dai; the Sui emperor granted it and also sent men to bestow wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: 3 Shabolu, khan of the Turks, sent his son to pay tribute to Sui and asked permission to hunt between Heng and Dai; the Sui emperor agreed and sent gifts of wine and food.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略帥部落再拜受賜。

translations.literal: Shabolu led his tribesmen in performing two bows to receive the gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Shabolu and his tribesmen bowed twice in accepting the gifts.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略尋卒，隋為之廢朝三日，遣太常弔祭。

translations.literal: Shabolu soon died; Sui suspended court for three days on his account and dispatched the Minister of Ceremonies to offer condolence sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Shabolu died shortly afterward; Sui canceled court for three days in mourning and sent the Minister of Ceremonies to perform condolence rites.

sentences.zh: 初，沙缽略以其子雍虞閭懦弱，遺令立其弟葉護處羅侯。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shabolu, because his son Yabghu Qagan was weak, left instructions that his brother Yehu Chuluohou should succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Shabolu, deeming his son Yabghu Qagan too soft, had left orders that his brother Yehu Chuluohou should take the throne.

sentences.zh: 雍虞閭遣使迎處羅侯，將立之，處羅侯曰：「我突厥自木杵可汗以來，多以弟代兄，以庶奪嫡，失先祖之法，不相敬畏。

translations.literal: Yabghu Qagan sent envoys to welcome Chuluohou and was about to install him; Chuluohou said: "Among us Turks, from the time of Khan Mucho onward, younger brothers have often replaced elder brothers and common-born sons have seized the succession from legitimate heirs, abandoning the ways of our ancestors and losing mutual reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Yabghu Qagan sent envoys to welcome Chuluohou and prepare to enthrone him; Chuluohou replied: "Since Khan Mucho's day our Turks have too often seen younger brothers supplant elders and bastards seize the succession — we have forsaken ancestral law and lost respect for one another.

sentences.zh: 汝當嗣位，我不憚拜汝！」

translations.literal: You should succeed to the throne — I do not shrink from bowing to you!"
translations.idiomatic: You are the rightful heir — I do not hesitate to bow before you!"

sentences.zh: 雍虞閭曰：「叔與我父，共根連體。

translations.literal: Yabghu Qagan said: "My uncle and my father share one root and one body.
translations.idiomatic: Yabghu Qagan replied: "My uncle and my father are of one root and one body.

sentences.zh: 我，枝葉也，豈可使根本反從枝葉，叔父屈於卑幼乎！

translations.literal: I am but the branches and leaves — how could the root be made to follow the branches and leaves, with my uncle bowing to the younger!
translations.idiomatic: I am but a branch — how can the root defer to the branch and make my uncle bow to his junior!

sentences.zh: 且亡父之命，何可廢也！

translations.literal: Moreover, my late father's command — how can it be set aside!
translations.idiomatic: And my late father's dying command — how can I disregard it!

sentences.zh: 願叔勿疑！」

translations.literal: I beg my uncle not to doubt!"
translations.idiomatic: I beg you, Uncle — have no doubt!"

sentences.zh: 遣使相讓者五六，處羅侯竟立，是為莫何可汗。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent back and forth in mutual refusal five or six times; in the end Chuluohou was installed, and he became known as Khan Mohe.
translations.idiomatic: They exchanged envoys five or six times, each insisting the other take the throne; in the end Chuluohou was installed as khan, known as Mohe Qagan.

sentences.zh: 以雍虞閭為葉護。

translations.literal: Yabghu Qagan was made Yehu.
translations.idiomatic: Yabghu Qagan was appointed Yehu (heir apparent).

sentences.zh: 遣使上表言狀。

translations.literal: Envoys were dispatched to submit a memorial reporting the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent with a memorial describing the succession.

sentences.zh: 隋使車騎將軍長孫晟持節拜之，賜以鼓吹、幡旗。

translations.literal: Sui sent the Chariot and Cavalry General Zhangsun Sheng bearing credentials to invest him, bestowing musical accompaniment and banner flags.
translations.idiomatic: Sui dispatched Zhangsun Sheng, General of Chariots and Cavalry, with imperial credentials to invest him, granting drums and banners.

sentences.zh: 莫何勇而有謀，以隋所賜旗鼓西擊阿波；

translations.literal: Mohe was brave and resourceful; using the drums and banners granted by Sui, he marched west to attack Apo;
translations.idiomatic: Mohe, brave and shrewd, led the drums and banners Sui had given him west to attack Apo;

sentences.zh: 阿波之眾以為得隋兵助之，多望風降附。

translations.literal: Apo's followers, believing they faced Sui troops aiding the attack, for the most part surrendered at the sight of the advancing force.
translations.idiomatic: Apo's followers, thinking Sui troops had come to his aid, surrendered in droves at the mere sight of Mohe's banners.

sentences.zh: 遂生擒阿波，上書請其死生之命。

translations.literal: He then captured Apo alive and submitted a memorial requesting the emperor's decision on whether Apo should live or die.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Apo alive and sent a memorial asking the emperor to decide Apo's fate.

sentences.zh: 隋主下其議，樂安公元諧請就彼梟首；

translations.literal: The Sui emperor referred the matter for discussion; Yuan Xie, Duke of Le'an, asked that Apo be beheaded on the spot;
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor took counsel; Yuan Xie, Duke of Le'an, urged beheading Apo where he stood;

sentences.zh: 武陽公李充請生取入朝，顯戮以示百姓。

translations.literal: Li Chong, Duke of Wuyang, asked that Apo be taken alive to the capital and publicly executed to show the people.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong, Duke of Wuyang, urged bringing Apo alive to the capital for a public execution as a warning.

sentences.zh: 隋主謂長孫晟：「於卿何如？」

translations.literal: The Sui emperor asked Zhangsun Sheng: "What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor asked Zhangsun Sheng: "What is your view?"

sentences.zh: 晟對曰：「若突厥背誕，須齊之以刑。

translations.literal: Sheng replied: "If the Turks betray their pledges, they must be brought into line by punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng replied: "When Turks breach their oaths, they must be disciplined by force.

sentences.zh: 今其昆弟自相夷滅，阿波之惡非負國家。

translations.literal: Now their brothers are destroying one another; Apo's wickedness is not a crime against the state.
translations.idiomatic: But now their brothers are destroying one another; Apo's offense is not treason against Sui.

sentences.zh: 因其困窮，取而為戮，恐非招遠之道。

translations.literal: To seize him in his distress and put him to death — I fear that is not the way to win over distant peoples.
translations.idiomatic: To seize him in his weakness and kill him would not be the way to win over distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 不如兩存之。」

translations.literal: It would be better to let both survive."
translations.idiomatic: Better to let them both live."

sentences.zh: 左僕射高熲曰：「骨肉相殘，教之蠹也，宜存養以示寬大。」

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Gao Bin said: "When kin slaughter one another, it is the bane of their teaching; they should be spared and nurtured to demonstrate magnanimity."
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Premier Gao Bin said: "Fratricide is a rot in their customs; sparing them will show our magnanimity."

sentences.zh: 隋主從之。

translations.literal: The Sui emperor followed their advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 4甲戌，隋遣兼散騎常侍楊同等來聘。

translations.literal: 4 On the day jiaxu, Sui dispatched Yang Tong, concurrent Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and others on a mission of friendship.
translations.idiomatic: 4 On jiaxu day Sui sent Yang Tong, concurrent Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and others on a friendly visit.

sentences.zh: 5五月，乙亥朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: 5 In the fifth month, on the first day of the month yihai, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: 5 In the fifth month, on the first day (yihai), there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 6秋，七月，己丑，隋衛昭王爽卒。

translations.literal: 6 In autumn, the seventh month, on the day jichou, Shuang, Prince Wei Zhao of Sui, died.
translations.idiomatic: 6 In autumn, the seventh month on jichou, Prince Wei Zhao Shuang of Sui died.

sentences.zh: 八月，隋主征梁主入朝。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Sui emperor summoned the Liang ruler to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Sui emperor summoned the ruler of Liang to the capital.

sentences.zh: 梁主帥其群臣二百餘人發江陵；

translations.literal: The Liang ruler set out from Jiangling with more than two hundred ministers and officials;
translations.idiomatic: The Liang ruler departed Jiangling with more than two hundred officials and ministers;

sentences.zh: 庚申，至長安。

translations.literal: on the day gengshen he arrived at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: arriving at Chang'an on gengshen day.

sentences.zh: 隋主以梁主在外，遣武鄉公崔弘度將兵戍江陵。

translations.literal: Because the Liang ruler was away, the Sui emperor dispatched Cui Hongdu, Duke of Wuxiang, to garrison Jiangling with troops.
translations.idiomatic: With the Liang ruler away, the Sui emperor sent Cui Hongdu, Duke of Wuxiang, to occupy Jiangling with troops.

sentences.zh: 軍至都州，梁主叔父太傅安平王巖、弟荊州刺史義興王□獻等恐弘度襲之，乙丑，遣其都官尚書沈君公詣荊州刺史宜黃侯慧紀請降。

translations.literal: When the army reached Du Province, the Liang ruler's uncle the Grand Tutor, Prince Anping Yan, and his brother the Governor of Jing Province, Prince of Yixing □ Xian, and others, fearing that Hongdu would attack, on the day yichou dispatched the Minister of Palace Affairs Shen Jungong to the Governor of Jing Province, Marquis of Yihuang Hui Ji, to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Du Province, the Liang ruler's uncle Grand Tutor Prince Anping Yan, his brother Jing Province governor Prince of Yixing □ Xian, and others, fearing attack, sent Minister of Palace Affairs Shen Jungong on yichou day to Hui Ji, governor of Jing Province and Marquis of Yihuang, offering surrender.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚寅，慧紀引兵至江陵城下。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day gengyin, Hui Ji led his troops to the foot of Jiangling's walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month on gengyin day Hui Ji marched his army to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，巖等驅文、武、男、女十萬口來奔。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, Yan and the others drove officials, soldiers, and men and women numbering a hundred thousand to flee to them.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day Yan and his allies drove a hundred thousand men, women, officials, and soldiers into flight toward them.

sentences.zh: 隋主聞之，廢梁國；

translations.literal: When the Sui emperor heard of it, he abolished the state of Liang;
translations.idiomatic: Learning of this, the Sui emperor dissolved the Liang state;

sentences.zh: 遣尚書左僕射高熲安集遺民；

translations.literal: he dispatched the Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Gao Bin to settle the remaining populace;
translations.idiomatic: he sent Left Vice Premier Gao Bin to pacify the displaced population;

sentences.zh: 梁中宗、世宗各給守塚十戶；

translations.literal: to the Middle and World Ancestors of Liang he granted ten households each to guard their tombs;
translations.idiomatic: he assigned ten tomb-guarding households each to Liang's Middle and World Ancestors;

sentences.zh: 拜梁主琮上柱國，賜爵莒公。

translations.literal: the Liang ruler Cong was appointed Grand General and enfeoffed as Duke of Ju.
translations.idiomatic: and ennobled the Liang ruler Cong as Grand General and Duke of Ju.

sentences.zh: 7甲午，大赦。

translations.literal: 7 On the day jiawu, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: 7 On jiawu day a general pardon was issued.

sentences.zh: 8冬，十月，隋主如同州；

translations.literal: 8 In winter, the tenth month, the Sui emperor went to Tong Province;
translations.idiomatic: 8 In winter, the tenth month, the Sui emperor traveled to Tongzhou;

sentences.zh: 癸亥，如蒲州。

translations.literal: on the day guihai he went to Pu Province.
translations.idiomatic: proceeding to Puzhou on guihai day.

sentences.zh: 9十一月，丙子，以蕭巖為開府儀同三司、東揚州刺史，蕭讞為吳州刺史。

translations.literal: 9 In the eleventh month, on the day bingzi, Xiao Yan was made Ceremonial Peer of the Third Rank with Opening Office and Governor of Eastern Yang Province, and Xiao Chen was made Governor of Wu Province.
translations.idiomatic: 9 In the eleventh month on bingzi day Xiao Yan was appointed third-rank ceremonial peer with open office and governor of Eastern Yangzhou, and Xiao Chen was made governor of Wu Province.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以豫章王叔英兼司徒。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, Prince of Yuzhang Shuying was additionally appointed Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day Prince Shuying of Yuzhang was made concurrent Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 10甲午，隋主如馮翊，親祠故社；

translations.literal: 10 On the day jiawu, the Sui emperor went to Pingyi and personally sacrificed at the old altars of soil and grain;
translations.idiomatic: 10 On jiawu day the Sui emperor traveled to Pingyi and personally offered sacrifice at the old communal altars;

sentences.zh: 戊戌，還長安。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, he returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu he returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 是行也，內史令李德林以疾不從，隋主自同州敕書追之，與議伐陳之計。

translations.literal: On this journey, Li Delin, Director of the Secretariat, did not accompany him due to illness; the Sui emperor sent an imperial letter from Tong Province summoning him back to discuss plans for attacking Chen.
translations.idiomatic: On this tour Li Delin, Director of the Secretariat, had stayed behind with illness; the Sui emperor sent an edict from Tong Province recalling him to deliberate the campaign against Chen.

sentences.zh: 及還，帝馬上舉鞭南指曰：「待平陳之日，以七寶裝嚴公，使自山以東無及公者。」

translations.literal: When they returned, the emperor on horseback raised his whip and pointed south, saying: "When the day comes that Chen is pacified, I shall adorn you, Lord, with the seven treasures, so that east of the mountains none can match you."
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey the emperor, still mounted, raised his whip and pointed south. "When Chen falls," he said, "I will adorn you with the seven treasures—you will have no peer east of the mountains."

sentences.zh: 初，隋主受禪以來，與陳鄰好甚篤，每獲陳諜，皆給衣馬禮遣之，而高宗猶不禁侵掠。

translations.literal: Earlier, since the Sui emperor had received the abdication, neighborly relations with Chen had been very close; whenever Chen spies were captured they were given clothing, horses, and gifts and sent away, yet Emperor Gao still did not forbid raids.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the Sui emperor took the throne, relations with Chen had remained cordial; captured Chen spies were always clothed, horsed, and sent home with gifts, yet Emperor Gao still permitted border raids.

sentences.zh: 故太建之末，隋師入寇；

translations.literal: Therefore at the end of the Taikian era, Sui armies invaded;
translations.idiomatic: Hence at the end of the Taikian reign Sui forces crossed the border;

sentences.zh: 會高宗殂，隋主即命班師，遣使赴吊，書稱姓名頓首。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao happened to die, the Sui emperor immediately ordered withdrawal of the army, dispatched envoys to offer condolences, and in his letter signed his name with a bow of the forehead to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao died soon after, the Sui emperor at once ordered the troops withdrawn and sent envoys of mourning; his letter bore his own name and a kowtow.

sentences.zh: 帝答之益驕，書末云：「想彼統內如宜，此宇宙清泰。」

translations.literal: The emperor replied with growing arrogance; at the end of his letter he wrote: "I trust affairs within your domain are as they should be; here under Heaven all is clear and tranquil."
translations.idiomatic: The Chen emperor's reply grew bolder; he ended his letter: "I trust all is well in your realm; here the cosmos is at peace."

sentences.zh: 隋主不悅，以示朝臣。

translations.literal: The Sui emperor was displeased and showed it to his court ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor was offended and showed the letter to his ministers.

sentences.zh: 上柱國楊素以為主辱臣死，再拜請罪。

translations.literal: Yang Su, Grand General, held that when the lord is insulted the minister must die; he bowed twice and begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Yang Su, holding that an insult to the sovereign demands a minister's life, bowed twice and pleaded for punishment.

sentences.zh: 隋主問取陳之策於高熲，對曰：「江北地寒，田收差晚；

translations.literal: The Sui emperor asked Gao Yong for a strategy to take Chen; he replied: "North of the river the land is cold and the harvest comes rather late;
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor asked Gao Yong how to conquer Chen. Gao Yong answered: "North of the Yangtze the land is cold and harvest comes late;

sentences.zh: 江南水田早熟。

translations.literal: South of the river the paddy fields ripen early.
translations.idiomatic: in the south the paddies ripen early.

sentences.zh: 量彼收穫之際，微征士馬，聲言掩襲，彼必屯兵守禦，足得廢其農時。

translations.literal: Calculate the time of their harvest, lightly mobilize troops and horses, and proclaim a surprise attack—they will surely mass soldiers to defend, which will be enough to waste their farming season.
translations.idiomatic: At harvest time, feign a small mobilization and proclaim a surprise raid—they will mass troops to defend and lose the farming season entirely.

sentences.zh: 彼既聚兵，我便解甲。

translations.literal: Once they have gathered their forces, we disband ours.
translations.idiomatic: Once they have gathered, we stand down.

sentences.zh: 再三若此，彼以為常；

translations.literal: Repeat this several times, and they will take it as routine;
translations.idiomatic: Do this again and again until they treat it as routine;

sentences.zh: 後更集兵，彼必不信。

translations.literal: Later when we again assemble troops, they surely will not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: then when we mobilize in earnest they will not believe us.

sentences.zh: 猶豫之頃，我乃濟師；

translations.literal: While they hesitate, we then cross our army over;
translations.idiomatic: In their moment of hesitation we cross the river;

sentences.zh: 登陸而戰，兵氣益倍。

translations.literal: Landing to fight, our soldiers' morale will be doubled.
translations.idiomatic: land and fight with morale twice what it would otherwise be.

sentences.zh: 又，江南土薄，捨多茅竹，所有儲積皆非地窖。

translations.literal: Further, south of the river the soil is thin, dwellings are mostly thatch and bamboo, and all stored provisions are not in underground cellars.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Jiangnan soil is thin; houses are mostly thatch and bamboo, and grain is stored above ground, not in cellars.

sentences.zh: 密遣行人因風縱火，待彼修立，復更燒之。

translations.literal: Secretly send agents to set fires when the wind is favorable; wait until they have rebuilt, then burn again.
translations.idiomatic: Send agents secretly to set fires when the wind serves; let them rebuild, then burn again.

sentences.zh: 不出數年，自可財力俱盡。」

translations.literal: Within a few years their wealth and strength will naturally be exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: In a few years their wealth and strength will be exhausted."

sentences.zh: 隋主用其策，陳人始困。

translations.literal: The Sui emperor adopted his strategy, and the Chen people began to be distressed.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor adopted the plan, and Chen began to suffer.

sentences.zh: 於是楊素、賀若弼及光州刺史高勱、虢州刺史崔仲方等爭獻平江南之策。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yang Su, He Ruo Bi, Gao Li Governor of Guang Province, Cui Zhongfang Governor of Guo Province, and others competed to submit strategies for pacifying Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yang Su, He Ruo Bi, Gao Li of Guang Province, Cui Zhongfang of Guo Province, and others vied to offer plans for conquering the south.

sentences.zh: 仲方上書曰：「今唯須武昌以下，蘄、和、滁、方、吳、海等州，更帖精兵，密營度計；

translations.literal: Zhongfang submitted a memorial saying: "Now we need only from Wuchang downstream—the provinces of Qi, He, Chu, Fang, Wu, Hai, and others—station elite troops afresh and secretly plan the campaign;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhongfang submitted a memorial: "From Wuchang downstream, in Qi, He, Chu, Fang, Wu, Hai, and the other provinces, we need only redeploy elite troops and plan the campaign in secret;

sentences.zh: 益、信、襄、荊、基、郢等州，速造舟楫，多張形勢，為水戰之具。

translations.literal: In Yi, Xin, Xiang, Jing, Ji, Ying, and other provinces, swiftly build boats and oars, display force broadly, and prepare equipment for naval warfare.
translations.idiomatic: in Yi, Xin, Xiang, Jing, Ji, Ying, and the rest, build ships quickly, show force on many fronts, and ready the means for river battle.

sentences.zh: 蜀、漢二江是其上流，水路衝要，必爭之所。

translations.literal: The Shu and Han Rivers are its upper reaches; the waterways are strategically vital—the place where contention is inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu and Han are the upper Yangtze—critical waterways and certain ground for a decisive contest.

sentences.zh: 賊雖於流頭、荊門、延洲、公安、巴陵、隱磯、夏首、蘄口、湓城置船，然終聚漢口、峽口，以水戰大決。

translations.literal: Though the enemy may station ships at Liutou, Jingmen, Yanzhou, Gong'an, Baling, Yinji, Xiashou, Qikou, and Pencheng, in the end they will mass at Hankou and Xiakou and decide the issue in a great naval battle.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy may station vessels at Liutou, Jingmen, Yanzhou, Gong'an, Baling, Yinji, Xiashou, Qikou, and Pencheng, but in the end they will concentrate at Hankou and Xiakou for the decisive river battle.

sentences.zh: 若賊必以上流有軍，令精兵赴援者，下流諸將即須擇便橫渡；

translations.literal: If the enemy, certain that there are troops upstream, sends elite forces to the rescue, our downstream generals must choose a favorable point and cross over;
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy sends elite troops upstream to reinforce, our downstream commanders must cross at the first good opportunity;

sentences.zh: 如擁眾自衛，上江水軍鼓行以前。

translations.literal: If they mass troops to defend themselves, our upstream navy will advance beating drums.
translations.idiomatic: if they hoard forces for defense, our upstream fleet will advance with drums beating.

sentences.zh: 彼雖恃九江、五湖之險，非德無以為固；

translations.literal: Though they rely on the perils of Jiujiang and the Five Lakes, without virtue they cannot hold firm;
translations.idiomatic: They may trust the defenses of Jiujiang and the Five Lakes, but without virtue no barrier holds;

sentences.zh: 徒有三吳、百越之兵，無恩不能自立矣。」

translations.literal: They merely have the troops of the Three Wu and the Hundred Yue—without benevolence they cannot stand on their own."
translations.idiomatic: they have the armies of Wu and Yue, but without grace they cannot endure."

sentences.zh: 隋主以仲方為基州刺史。

translations.literal: The Sui emperor made Zhongfang governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor appointed Cui Zhongfang governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 及受蕭巖等降，隋主益忿，謂高熲曰：「我為民父母，豈可限一衣帶水不拯之乎！」

translations.literal: When Xiao Yan and others surrendered, the Sui emperor grew angrier still; he said to Gao Yong: "I am parent to the people—how can I be confined by a belt of water and not rescue them!"
translations.idiomatic: After receiving the surrender of Xiao Yan and his fellows, the Sui emperor's wrath deepened. He told Gao Yong: "I am father and mother to the people—how can a strip of water keep me from saving them!"

sentences.zh: 命大作戰船。

translations.literal: He ordered the large-scale building of warships.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered warships built on a great scale.

sentences.zh: 人請密之，隋主曰：「吾將顯行天誅，何密之有！」

translations.literal: Some asked that it be kept secret; the Sui emperor said: "I intend to execute Heaven's punishment openly—what need for secrecy!"
translations.idiomatic: When some urged secrecy, the Sui emperor said: "I mean to carry out Heaven's judgment in the open—why hide it!"

sentences.zh: 使投其柿於江，曰：「若彼懼而能改，吾復何求！」

translations.literal: He had the hull timbers cast into the river and said: "If they fear this and reform, what more do I want!"
translations.idiomatic: He had the keels thrown into the river, saying: "If they take fright and mend their ways, what more could I ask!"

sentences.zh: 楊素在永安，造大艦，名曰「五牙」。

translations.literal: Yang Su at Yong'an built great ships called "Five-Tooth."
translations.idiomatic: At Yong'an Yang Su built great warships called the Five-Tooth.

sentences.zh: 上起樓五層，高百餘尺；

translations.literal: Above them he raised towers of five stories, over a hundred feet high;
translations.idiomatic: Each bore five-story towers more than a hundred feet tall;

sentences.zh: 左右前後置六拍竿，並高五十尺，容戰士八百人；

translations.literal: On left, right, front, and rear he placed six battering poles, each fifty feet high, holding eight hundred warriors;
translations.idiomatic: with six battering poles fifty feet high on every side, each vessel carrying eight hundred fighters;

sentences.zh: 次曰「黃龍」，置兵百人。

translations.literal: Next came those called "Yellow Dragon," with a hundred soldiers aboard.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the Yellow Dragon class, with a hundred men each.

sentences.zh: 自餘平乘、舴艋各有等差。

translations.literal: The remaining patrol boats and skiffs each had their grades.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser patrol boats and skiffs filled out the fleet in ranked sizes.

sentences.zh: 晉州刺史皇甫續將之官，稽首言陳有三可滅。

translations.literal: Huangfu Xu, governor of Jin Province, about to take up his post, bowed with his forehead to the ground and said Chen had three reasons why it could be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Xu, newly appointed governor of Jin Province, kowtowed and declared three reasons Chen could be conquered.

sentences.zh: 帝問其狀，曰：「大吞小，一也；

translations.literal: The emperor asked the particulars; he said: "The large swallowing the small—that is the first;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked what he meant. He said: "The great swallowing the small—first;

sentences.zh: 以有道伐無道，二也；

translations.literal: The righteous attacking the unrighteous—that is the second;
translations.idiomatic: the righteous overthrowing the wicked—second;

sentences.zh: 納叛臣蕭巖，於我有詞，三也。

translations.literal: Harboring the rebel minister Xiao Yan—we have right on our side—that is the third.
translations.idiomatic: their sheltering the rebel Xiao Yan gives us cause—third.

sentences.zh: 陛下若命將出師，臣願展絲發之效！」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty orders generals to march, this subject is willing to offer even the effort of a hair's breadth!"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty sends armies forth, I will serve even unto my last breath!"

sentences.zh: 隋主勞而遣之。

translations.literal: The Sui emperor thanked him and sent him on his way.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor commended him and sent him to his post.

sentences.zh: 時江南妖異特眾，臨平湖草久塞，忽然自開。

translations.literal: At that time portents and anomalies in Jiangnan were especially numerous; the grass of Linping Lake, long choked up, suddenly cleared by itself.
translations.idiomatic: Omens multiplied in Jiangnan; the grass-choked Linping Lake suddenly cleared of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 帝惡之，乃自賣於佛寺為奴以厭之。

translations.literal: The emperor hated this and sold himself into slavery at a Buddhist temple to dispel it.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen emperor took this as ill omen and sold himself as a slave to a temple to avert it.

sentences.zh: 又於建康造大皇寺，起七級浮圖；

translations.literal: He also built the Great Imperial Temple at Jiankang and erected a seven-story pagoda;
translations.idiomatic: He also built the Great Imperial Temple in Jiankang and raised a seven-tier pagoda;

sentences.zh: 未畢，火從中起而焚之。

translations.literal: Before it was finished, fire arose from within and burned it down.
translations.idiomatic: Before it was finished fire broke out within and consumed it.

sentences.zh: 11吳興章華，好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: 11 Zhang Hua of Wuxing loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: 11 Zhang Hua of Wuxing was a devoted scholar and accomplished writer.

sentences.zh: 朝臣以華素無伐閱，競排詆之，除大市令。

translations.literal: Court ministers, because Hua had no record of military merit, competed to slander him and had him appointed market magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhang Hua had no martial pedigree, court rivals slandered him until he was demoted to market magistrate.

sentences.zh: 華鬱鬱不得志，上書極諫，略曰：「昔高祖南平百越，北誅逆虜，世祖東定吳會，西破王琳，高宗克復淮南，闢地千里，三祖之功勤亦至矣。

translations.literal: Hua, depressed and unfulfilled, submitted a fierce memorial of remonstrance; in summary he wrote: "In the past Grand Ancestor pacified the Hundred Yue in the south and executed the rebel barbarians in the north; World Ancestor settled Wu and Kuaiji in the east and defeated Wang Lin in the west; High Ancestor recovered Huainan and opened territory a thousand li—the toil and merit of the three ancestors reached its utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Bitter and thwarted, Zhang Hua submitted a stern memorial of remonstrance. In part he wrote: "Grand Ancestor pacified the Hundred Yue in the south and destroyed northern rebels; World Ancestor secured Wu and Kuaiji in the east and broke Wang Lin in the west; High Ancestor recovered Huainan and opened lands a thousand li—the three founding emperors toiled beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位，於今五年，不思先帝之艱難，不知天命之可畏；

translations.literal: Your Majesty has been on the throne five years to this day, yet does not reflect on the hardships of the Former Emperor, nor understand that Heaven's mandate inspires awe;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has reigned five years and still gives no thought to your father's hardships or to the dread weight of Heaven's mandate;

sentences.zh: 溺於嬖寵，惑於酒色；

translations.literal: You drown in favorites and are befuddled by wine and women;
translations.idiomatic: you drown in favorites and lose yourself in wine and women;

sentences.zh: 祠七廟而不出，拜三妃而臨軒；

translations.literal: You sacrifice at the seven temples without attending in person, yet greet three consorts from the imperial dais;
translations.idiomatic: you send others to the ancestral temples while you receive three consorts from the throne;

sentences.zh: 老臣宿將棄之草莽，諂佞讒邪升之朝廷。

translations.literal: Old ministers and veteran generals are cast aside into the weeds, while flatterers, sycophants, and malicious men are raised into the court.
translations.idiomatic: Veteran ministers and generals languish in obscurity while sycophants and schemers rise to court;

sentences.zh: 今疆場日蹙，隋軍壓境，陛下如不改弦易張，臣見麋鹿復游於姑蘇矣！」

translations.literal: Now the borders shrink daily and Sui troops press upon the frontier; if Your Majesty does not change course and retune the strings, this subject sees deer roaming Gusu once again!"
translations.idiomatic: The frontiers shrink daily and Sui armies press the border—unless Your Majesty changes course, I foresee deer grazing once more in the ruins of Gusu!"

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，即日斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious and had him beheaded that very day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and had him executed the same day.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，辛巳，立皇子為東陽王，恬為錢塘王。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, on the day xinsi, a prince was installed as Prince of Dongyang, and Tian was installed as Prince of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring, first month, on xinsi day a prince was made Prince of Dongyang and Tian was made Prince of Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 遣散騎常侍袁雅等聘於隋；

translations.literal: Yuan Ya, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and others were sent on a mission of friendship to Sui;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ya, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and others were dispatched on a friendly mission to Sui;

sentences.zh: 又遣騎常侍九江周羅□將兵屯峽口，侵隋峽州。

translations.literal: He also sent Zhou Luo□ of Jiujiang, Regular Attendant of Cavalry, to lead troops stationed at Xiakou and raid Sui's Xia Province.
translations.idiomatic: And Zhou Luo□ of Jiujiang, Regular Attendant of Cavalry, was sent to garrison Xiakou with troops and raid Sui's Xia Province.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲戌，隋遣兼散騎常侍程尚賢等來聘。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day jiaxu, Sui dispatched Cheng Shangxian, concurrent Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and others on a mission of friendship.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month on jiaxu day Sui sent Cheng Shangxian, concurrent Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and others on a friendly visit.

sentences.zh: 2戊寅，隋主下詔曰：「陳叔寶據手掌之地，恣溪壑之欲，劫奪閭閻，資產俱竭，驅逼內外，勞役弗已；

translations.literal: 2 On the day wuyin, the Sui emperor issued an edict saying: "Chen Shubao occupies a palm-sized territory yet indulges desires like ravines and gullies; he plunders households until assets are exhausted, drives and coerces inner and outer alike, and labor and corvée never cease;
translations.idiomatic: 2 On wuyin day the Sui emperor proclaimed an edict: "Chen Shubao holds a handbreadth of land yet gorges like a glutton; he robs the people until nothing is left, presses nobles and commoners alike into endless labor,

sentences.zh: 窮奢極侈，俾晝作夜；

translations.literal: He exhausts extravagance and extreme luxury, making day into night;
translations.idiomatic: squanders wealth in boundless excess and turns day into night;

sentences.zh: 斬直言之客，滅無罪之家；

translations.literal: He executes guests who speak plainly and exterminates innocent families;
translations.idiomatic: executes those who speak plainly and destroys guiltless households;

sentences.zh: 欺天造惡，祭鬼求恩；

translations.literal: He deceives Heaven and creates evil, sacrificing to ghosts to beg for favor;
translations.idiomatic: defies Heaven with wicked deeds and bribes ghosts for favor;

sentences.zh: 盛粉黛而執干戈，曳羅綺而呼警蹕；

translations.literal: He arrays rouge and powder yet grasps weapons, trails silk and brocade yet calls out the imperial guard;
translations.idiomatic: paints his face and takes up arms, drags silks and brocades yet shouts for the imperial procession;

sentences.zh: 自古昏亂，罕或能比。

translations.literal: Since antiquity among the deluded and chaotic, few can compare.
translations.idiomatic: Among the dissolute rulers of history, few rival him.

sentences.zh: 君子潛逃，小人得志。

translations.literal: Worthy men flee in hiding; petty men achieve their ambition.
translations.idiomatic: The worthy flee into hiding; the base flourish.

sentences.zh: 天災地孽，物怪人妖。

translations.literal: Heaven sends disasters, earth breeds calamities, things become monstrous, and men turn demonic.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sends disasters, earth breeds portents, things turn uncanny, men grow monstrous.

sentences.zh: 衣冠鉗口，道路以目。

translations.literal: The gentry clamp their mouths shut; on the roads people exchange looks.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars dare not speak; travelers dare only exchange glances.

sentences.zh: 重以背德違言，搖蕩疆場；

translations.literal: Add to this violation of virtue and breach of pledges, and agitation along the borders;
translations.idiomatic: To this he adds broken faith and border provocations;

sentences.zh: 晝伏夜遊，鼠竊狗盜。

translations.literal: Hiding by day and raiding by night like rats and thieves.
translations.idiomatic: skulking by day and raiding by night like rats and dogs.

sentences.zh: 天之所覆，無非朕臣，每關聽覽，有懷傷惻。

translations.literal: All under Heaven's canopy are none other than my subjects; whenever this comes to my hearing, I am moved to compassionate grief.
translations.idiomatic: All beneath Heaven are my subjects; each report fills me with sorrow and pity.

sentences.zh: 可出師授律，應機誅殄；

translations.literal: Let armies be dispatched with the martial code, and at the opportune moment execute extermination;
translations.idiomatic: Let armies march under the code of war and destroy the enemy at the fitting hour;

sentences.zh: 在斯一舉，永清吳越。」

translations.literal: In this single campaign Wu and Yue will be forever pacified."
translations.idiomatic: in one stroke Wu and Yue will be pacified forever."

sentences.zh: 又送璽書暴帝二十惡；

translations.literal: He also sent an imperial letter enumerating the emperor's twenty crimes;
translations.idiomatic: He also sent an imperial letter listing twenty of the emperor's crimes;

sentences.zh: 仍散寫詔書三十萬紙，遍諭江外。

translations.literal: And had three hundred thousand copies of the edict made and distributed, proclaiming it throughout the lands beyond the river.
translations.idiomatic: and had three hundred thousand copies circulated south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 太子胤，性聰敏，好文學，然頗有過失；

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yin was intelligent by nature and loved literature, yet had considerable faults;
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yin was bright and devoted to letters, but prone to missteps;

sentences.zh: 詹事袁憲切諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yuan Xian remonstrated sharply, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Yuan Xian admonished him sternly, without effect.

sentences.zh: 時沈后無寵，而近侍左右數於東宮往來，太子亦數使人至后所，帝疑其怨望，甚惡之。

translations.literal: At this time Empress Shen had no favor, yet attendants of the inner court frequently passed to and fro with the Eastern Palace, and the crown prince also often sent men to the empress's quarters; the emperor suspected resentment and greatly detested this.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Shen had fallen from favor, yet court attendants still frequented the Eastern Palace and the prince often sent messengers to her quarters; the emperor suspected conspiracy and loathed it.

sentences.zh: 張、孔二貴妃日夜構成后及太子之短，孔范之徒又於外助之。

translations.literal: The two honored consorts Zhang and Kong day and night wove faults of the empress and crown prince; Kong Fan's faction also assisted from outside.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts Zhang and Kong worked day and night to blacken the empress and prince; Kong Fan and his allies abetted them from without.

sentences.zh: 帝欲立張貴妃子始安王深為嗣，嘗從容言之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to install Prince Shen of Shi'an, son of Consort Zhang, as heir, and once spoke of it at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to make Prince Shen of Shi'an, Consort Zhang's son, heir, and once mentioned it casually.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書蔡征順旨稱讚，袁憲厲色折之曰：「皇太子，國家儲副，億兆宅心，卿是何人，輕言廢立！」

translations.literal: Cai Zheng, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, praised this to suit the emperor's wish; Yuan Xian with stern countenance rebutted him, saying: "The crown prince is the state's heir designate, in whom the myriad people place their hearts—who are you to lightly speak of deposing and establishing!"
translations.idiomatic: Cai Zheng, Minister of Personnel, flattered the notion; Yuan Xian rebuked him sharply: "The crown prince is the nation's heir—the people look to him—who are you to speak lightly of deposing him!"

sentences.zh: 帝卒從征議。

translations.literal: In the end the emperor followed Zheng's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the emperor sided with Cai Zheng.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，庚子，廢太子胤為吳興王，立揚州刺史始安王深為太子。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on the day gengzi, Crown Prince Yin was deposed and made Prince of Wuxing, and Prince Shen of Shi'an, governor of Yang Province, was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, fifth month, on gengzi day Crown Prince Yin was demoted to Prince of Wuxing and Prince Shen of Shi'an, governor of Yang Province, was made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 征，景歷之子也。

translations.literal: Zheng was the son of Jingli.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Zheng was the son of Cai Jingli.

sentences.zh: 深亦聰惠，有志操，容止儼然，雖左右近侍未嘗見其喜慍。

translations.literal: Shen was also intelligent and perceptive, possessed moral resolve, and in bearing was dignified; even close attendants never saw him show joy or anger.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was likewise bright and principled, grave in manner; even his closest attendants never saw him show pleasure or anger.

sentences.zh: 帝聞袁憲嘗諫胤，即日用憲為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard that Yuan Xian had once remonstrated on Yin's behalf, he immediately made Yuan Xian Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs that same day.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Yuan Xian had defended Yin, the emperor that same day made him Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝遇沈后素薄，張貴妃專後宮之政，後澹然，未嘗有所忌怨，身居儉約，衣服無錦繡之飾，唯尋閱圖史及釋典為事，數上書諫爭。

translations.literal: The emperor had always treated Empress Shen coldly; Consort Zhang monopolized governance of the inner palace. The empress was serene, never harboring jealousy or resentment; she lived frugally, her clothing without brocade or embroidery, devoting herself only to reading histories and Buddhist scriptures, and repeatedly submitted memorials of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long treated Empress Shen coldly while Consort Zhang ruled the inner palace. The empress remained serene, never jealous; she lived simply, wore no silk or brocade, passed her days reading history and Buddhist texts, and repeatedly submitted remonstrances.

sentences.zh: 帝欲廢之而立張貴妃，會國亡，不果。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to depose her and install Consort Zhang, but when the state fell it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to depose her and elevate Consort Zhang, but the kingdom fell before he could.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己亥，立皇子蕃為吳郡王。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jihai, the emperor's son Fan was installed as Prince of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, tenth month, on jihai day the emperor's son Fan was made Prince of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 3己未，隋置淮南行省於壽春，以晉王廣為尚書令。

translations.literal: 3 On the day jiwei, Sui established the Huainan Branch Secretariat at Shouchun and made Prince of Jin Guang Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: 3 On jiwei day Sui established a Huainan branch secretariat at Shouchun and appointed Prince Guang of Jin as its director.

sentences.zh: 帝遣兼散騎常侍王琬、兼通直散騎常侍許善心聘於隋，隋人留於客館。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Wang Wan, concurrent Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and Xu Shanshan, concurrent Direct Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, on a mission of friendship to Sui; the Sui people detained them in the guest lodge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Wang Wan, concurrent Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and Xu Shanshan, concurrent Direct Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, on a diplomatic mission to Sui; the Sui detained them in the guest lodge.

sentences.zh: 琬等屢請還，不聽。

translations.literal: Wan and the others repeatedly requested to return, but were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Wan and his party repeatedly asked to go home, but were refused.

sentences.zh: 甲子，隋以出師，有事於太廟，命晉王廣、秦王俊、清河公楊素皆為行軍元帥。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, as Sui was about to march out, it performed rites at the Imperial Temple and appointed the Prince of Jin, Guang, the Prince of Qin, Jun, and the Duke of Qinghe, Yang Su, all as campaign marshals.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day, as Sui prepared to take the field, the emperor performed rites at the Imperial Temple and named the Prince of Jin Guang, the Prince of Qin Jun, and Duke of Qinghe Yang Su campaign marshals.

sentences.zh: 廣出六合，俊出襄陽，素出永安，荊州刺史劉仁恩出江陵，蘄州刺史王世積出蘄春，廬州總管韓擒虎出廬江，吳州總管賀若弼出廣陵，青州總管弘農燕榮出東海，凡總管九十，兵五十一萬八千，皆受晉王節度。

translations.literal: Guang marched out from Liuhe, Jun from Xiangyang, Su from Yong'an, Jingzhou governor Liu Ren'en from Jiangling, Qizhou governor Wang Shiji from Qichun, Luzhou inspector-general Han Qihu from Lujiang, Wuzhou inspector-general He Ruo from Guangling, Qingzhou inspector-general Yan Rong of Hongnong from the Eastern Sea—in all ninety inspector-generals and 518,000 troops, all under the Prince of Jin's command.
translations.idiomatic: Guang advanced from Liuhe, Jun from Xiangyang, Su from Yong'an, Liu Ren'en of Jingzhou from Jiangling, Wang Shiji of Qizhou from Qichun, Han Qihu of Luzhou from Lujiang, He Ruo of Wuzhou from Guangling, and Yan Rong of Hongnong from the Eastern Sea—ninety commanders in all, 518,000 men, all under the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 東接滄海，西拒巴、蜀，旌旗舟楫，橫亙數千里。

translations.literal: Eastward they reached the Bohai Sea; westward they faced Ba and Shu; banners, flags, boats, and oars stretched unbroken for thousands of li.
translations.idiomatic: Their line ran east to the Bohai Sea and west toward Ba and Shu; banners and fleets stretched thousands of li without break.

sentences.zh: 以左僕射高熲為晉王元師長史，右僕射王韶為司馬，軍中事皆取決焉；

translations.literal: The Left Vice Director Gao Yong was made chief aide to the Prince of Jin as marshal, and the Right Vice Director Wang Shao was made chief of staff; all military affairs were decided through them;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yong, Left Vice Director, was made chief of staff to the Prince of Jin, and Wang Shao, Right Vice Director, was made chief secretary; all military decisions ran through them;

sentences.zh: 區處支度，無所凝滯。

translations.literal: the disposition of divisions and supplies met with no delay.
translations.idiomatic: and the allocation of forces and supplies never stalled.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁卯，隋主親餞將士；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day dingmao, the Sui emperor personally saw off the troops;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month on dingmao day the Sui emperor personally saw the army off;

sentences.zh: 乙亥，至定城，陳師誓眾。

translations.literal: on the day yihai he reached Dingcheng, arrayed the army, and swore an oath before the host.
translations.idiomatic: on yihai he reached Dingcheng, drew up the army, and addressed the troops.

sentences.zh: 4丙子，立皇弟叔榮為新昌王，叔匡為太原王。

translations.literal: 4 On the day bingzi he installed his younger brother Shurong as Prince of Xinchang and Shukuang as Prince of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: 4 On bingzi day he made his younger brothers Shurong Prince of Xinchang and Shukuang Prince of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 5隋主如河東；

translations.literal: 5 The Sui emperor went to Hedong;
translations.idiomatic: 5 The Sui emperor traveled to Hedong;

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚子，還長安。

translations.literal: in the twelfth month, on the day gengzi, he returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: in the twelfth month on gengzi day he returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 突厥莫何可汗西擊鄰國，中流矢而卒。

translations.literal: The Turkic Mohe Kaghan attacked a western neighboring state and died midstream from an arrow wound.
translations.idiomatic: The Turkic Mohe Kaghan attacked a western neighbor and was struck by an arrow and died in the field.

sentences.zh: 國人立雍虞閭，號頡伽施多那都藍可汗。

translations.literal: The people installed Yongyulü and styled him Kaghan Jiagshiduonadu.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks raised Yongyulü to the throne as Kaghan Jiagshiduonadu.

sentences.zh: 6隋軍臨江，高熲謂行台吏部郎中薛道衡曰：「今茲大舉，江東必可克乎？」

translations.literal: 6 As the Sui army reached the Yangtze, Gao Yong said to Xue Daohang, Director in the Ministry of Personnel of the Field Secretariat: "With this great campaign, can Jiangdong surely be taken?"
translations.idiomatic: 6 When the Sui army reached the Yangtze, Gao Yong asked Xue Daohang of the Field Secretariat's Ministry of Personnel: "With this full-scale campaign, can we take Jiangdong?"

sentences.zh: 道衡曰：「克之。

translations.literal: Daohang said: "It can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Daohang answered: "We can take it.

sentences.zh: 嘗聞郭璞有言：『江東分王三百年，復與中國合。』

translations.literal: I once heard Guo Pu say: 'East of the River will divide kings for three hundred years, then reunite with the Central States.'
translations.idiomatic: I once heard Guo Pu say: 'The lands east of the Yangtze will be ruled separately for three hundred years, then reunite with the heartland.'

sentences.zh: 今此數將周，一也。

translations.literal: Now that number is nearly complete—that is the first point.
translations.idiomatic: That span is nearly complete—first.

sentences.zh: 主上恭儉勤勞，叔寶荒淫驕侈，二也。

translations.literal: Our lord is reverent, frugal, and diligent, while Shubao is dissolute, extravagant, and arrogant—that is the second.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign is reverent, frugal, and tireless, while Chen Shubao is dissolute, arrogant, and wasteful—second.

sentences.zh: 國之安危在所寄任，彼以江總為相，唯事詩酒，拔小人施文慶，委以政事，蕭摩訶、任蠻奴為大將，皆一夫之用耳，三也。

translations.literal: A state's safety or peril depends on those entrusted with office; they have Jiang Zong as chancellor and devote themselves only to poetry and wine, they promote the petty man Shi Wenqing and entrust him with government, and they make Xiao Mohe and Ren Mannu great generals—all men of limited use—that is the third.
translations.idiomatic: A state's fate rests on those it appoints; they have Jiang Zong as chancellor and care only for wine and verse, they elevate the petty Shi Wenqing to govern affairs, and they put Xiao Mohe and Ren Mannu in command—all men of narrow talent—third.

sentences.zh: 我有道而大，彼無德而小，量其甲士不過十萬，西自巫峽，東至滄海，分之則勢懸而力弱，聚之則守此而失彼，四也。

translations.literal: We possess the Way and are great; they lack virtue and are small; I estimate their armored soldiers at no more than one hundred thousand; from Wuxia in the west to the Bohai Sea in the east, if divided their situation hangs in the balance and their strength is weak, if gathered they must defend here and lose there—that is the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: We have the Way and are mighty; they lack virtue and are small; their armored troops cannot exceed one hundred thousand; from Wuxia Gorge west to the Bohai Sea east, divided they are overextended and weak, gathered they cannot hold every point—fourth.

sentences.zh: 席捲之勢，事在不疑。」

translations.literal: With a sweeping momentum, the outcome admits no doubt."
translations.idiomatic: Once the tide rolls in, the outcome is not in doubt."

sentences.zh: 熲欣然曰：「得君言成敗之理，令人豁然。

translations.literal: Gao Yong said with pleasure: "Hearing your words on the logic of success and failure makes everything suddenly clear.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yong said gladly: "Your account of why we shall prevail clears the mind at once.

sentences.zh: 本以才學相期，不意籌略乃爾。」

translations.literal: I originally looked to you for talent and learning, and did not expect your strategic insight to be like this."
translations.idiomatic: I valued you for scholarship, not knowing your strategic judgment ran so deep."

sentences.zh: 秦王俊督諸軍國屯漢口，為上流節度。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin, Jun, supervised the armies of the realm encamped at Hankou as commander of the upper Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qin Jun commanded the allied armies encamped at Hankou, directing the upper Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 詔以散騎常侍周羅□都督巴峽緣江諸軍事以拒之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Zhou Luo□, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, to oversee all military affairs along the Ba-Xia stretch of the river to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named Zhou Luo□, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, commander of all forces along the Ba-Xia riverfront, to hold them off.

sentences.zh: 楊素引舟師下三峽，軍至流頭灘。

translations.literal: Yang Su led the fleet down the Three Gorges, and the army reached Liutoutan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su led his fleet through the Three Gorges as far as Liutoutan.

sentences.zh: 將軍戚昕以青龍百餘艘、守狼尾灘，地勢險峭，隋人患之。

translations.literal: The general Qi Xin, with more than one hundred Green Dragon ships, defended Langwei Beach; the ground was steep and perilous, and the Sui men were troubled by it.
translations.idiomatic: General Qi Xin held Langwei Beach with more than a hundred Green Dragon ships; the ground was steep and treacherous, and the Sui commanders worried over it.

sentences.zh: 素曰：「勝負大計，在此一舉。

translations.literal: Su said: "Victory and defeat in the grand design turn on this one move.
translations.idiomatic: Su said: "The whole campaign turns on this one stroke.

sentences.zh: 若晝日下船，彼見我虛實，灘流迅激，制不由人，則吾失其便；

translations.literal: If we disembark by day, they will see our true strength; the current in the rapids is swift and control is not in our hands, and we will lose our advantage;
translations.idiomatic: If we land by day they will see our strength; the rapids run too fast for us to control, and we will lose the advantage;

sentences.zh: 不如以夜掩之。」

translations.literal: it would be better to cover our approach under night."
translations.idiomatic: better to strike under cover of night."

sentences.zh: 素新帥黃龍數千艘，銜枚而下，遣開府儀同三司王長襲引步卒自南岸擊昕別柵，大將軍劉仁恩帥甲騎自北岸趣白沙，遲明而至，擊之；

translations.literal: Su newly commanded several thousand Yellow Dragon ships and descended with gags in the men's mouths; he dispatched Wang Changxi, Honorary Grand Master of the Palace with the Third Rank of Honor, to lead infantry from the south bank against Xin's separate fort, and the Great General Liu Ren'en to lead armored cavalry from the north bank toward Baisha; at dawn they arrived and attacked;
translations.idiomatic: Su led several thousand fresh Yellow Dragon ships downstream with the men gagged; he sent Wang Changxi, Honorary Grand Master of the Palace with the Third Rank of Honor, to strike Xin's outpost from the south bank with infantry, and Great General Liu Ren'en to rush Baisha from the north bank with armored cavalry; at dawn they fell upon the enemy;

sentences.zh: 昕敗走，悉俘其眾，勞而遣之，秋毫不犯。

translations.literal: Xin was defeated and fled; they captured his entire force, thanked them and sent them away, and did not violate so much as a hair.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Xin was routed and fled; his whole force was taken, then thanked and released without the least harm.

sentences.zh: 素帥水軍東下，舟艫被江，旌甲曜日。

translations.literal: Su led the navy eastward; boats covered the river, and banners and armor gleamed in the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Su drove his fleet east; the river was packed with ships, banners and armor blazing in the sun.

sentences.zh: 素坐平乘大船，容貌雄偉，陳人望之，皆懼，曰：「清河公即江神也！」

translations.literal: Su sat aboard a great flat-decked vessel, his bearing imposing; the Chen people who looked upon him were all afraid and said: "The Duke of Qinghe is the River God!"
translations.idiomatic: Su stood on a great flat-decked ship, imposing in bearing; the Chen soldiers who saw him were terrified and cried: "The Duke of Qinghe is the god of the river!"

sentences.zh: 江濱鎮戍聞隋軍將至，相繼奏聞；

translations.literal: River garrisons, hearing that the Sui army was about to arrive, reported in succession;
translations.idiomatic: River garrisons, hearing the Sui army was near, sent report after report;

sentences.zh: 施文慶、沈客卿並抑而不言。

translations.literal: Shi Wenqing and Shen Keqing both suppressed the news and said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: but Shi Wenqing and Shen Keqing buried each report and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 初，上以蕭巖、蕭讞，梁之宗室，擁眾來奔，心忌之，故遠散其眾，以巖為東揚州刺史，讞為吳州刺史；

translations.literal: Initially, because Xiao Yan and Xiao Chen, members of the Liang imperial house, had brought their followers in surrender, the emperor was jealous at heart; he therefore scattered their followers far away, appointing Yan governor of East Yangzhou and Chen governor of Wu;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had been wary of Xiao Yan and Xiao Chen, Liang princes who had defected with their followers; he had scattered their men and posted Yan to East Yangzhou and Chen to Wu;

sentences.zh: 使領軍任忠出守吳興郡，以襟帶二州。

translations.literal: he made the Commandant of the Guard Ren Zhong go out to guard Wuxing commandery, to gird the two provinces.
translations.idiomatic: he sent Commandant of the Guard Ren Zhong to hold Wuxing and link the two provinces.

sentences.zh: 使南平王嶷鎮江州，永嘉王彥鎮南徐州。

translations.literal: He made the Prince of Nanping, Liao, guard Jiangzhou, and the Prince of Yongjia, Yan, guard South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He posted Prince of Nanping Liao at Jiangzhou and Prince of Yongjia Yan at South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋召二王赴明年元會，命緣江諸防船艦悉從二王還都，為威勢以示梁人之來者。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he summoned both princes to the New Year's assembly of the coming year and ordered that all defensive ships along the river follow the two princes back to the capital, as a show of might for Liang men who might come over.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned both princes to the coming New Year's court and ordered every river-defense ship to return with them to the capital, to impress would-be Liang defectors.

sentences.zh: 由是江中無一斗船，上流諸州兵皆阻楊素軍，不得至。

translations.literal: By this there was not a single fighting ship on the river, and the troops of the upper provinces were all blocked by Yang Su's army and could not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Thus not one warship remained on the Yangtze, and upstream provincial troops were all blocked by Yang Su and never reached the front.

sentences.zh: 湘州刺史晉熙王叔文，在職既久，大得人和，上以其據有上流，陰忌之；

translations.literal: The Xiangzhou governor, the Prince of Jinxi, Shuwen, had long held office and greatly won men's hearts; because he held the upper Yangtze the emperor secretly envied him;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jinxi Shuwen, governor of Xiangzhou, had long held his post and won deep loyalty; because he controlled the upper Yangtze the emperor secretly feared him;

sentences.zh: 自度素與群臣少恩，恐不為用，無可任者，乃擢施文慶為都督、湘州刺史，配以精兵二千，欲令西上；

translations.literal: reckoning that Su had shown little favor to the ministers and fearing he would not be used, and finding no one else fit for appointment, he promoted Shi Wenqing to be commander and governor of Xiangzhou, assigning him two thousand picked troops, intending to send him west;
translations.idiomatic: judging that Yang Su owed the court ministers little loyalty and might not serve them well, and seeing no better choice, he made Shi Wenqing commander and governor of Xiangzhou with two thousand elite troops and ordered him upstream;

sentences.zh: 仍征叔文還朝。

translations.literal: he also summoned Shuwen back to court.
translations.idiomatic: and recalled Shuwen to the capital.

sentences.zh: 文慶深喜其事，然懼出外之後，執事者持己短長，因進其黨沈客卿以自代。

translations.literal: Wenqing was deeply pleased by the appointment, yet feared that once he left the capital those in charge would seize on his faults; he therefore advanced his ally Shen Keqing to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqing welcomed the post but feared rivals at court would use his absence against him, so he put his ally Shen Keqing forward to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 未發間，二人共掌機密。

translations.literal: Before he set out, the two men together controlled state secrets.
translations.idiomatic: Before he departed the two men held the reins of power between them.

sentences.zh: 護軍將軍樊毅言於僕射袁憲曰：「京口、採石俱是要地，各須銳兵五千，並出金翅二百，緣江上下，以為防備。」

translations.literal: The Colonel of the Guard Fan Yi said to the Vice Director Yuan Xian: "Jingkou and Caishi are both critical points; each needs five thousand crack troops, and two hundred Golden Wing ships deployed up and down the river as defense."
translations.idiomatic: Colonel of the Guard Fan Yi told Vice Director Yuan Xian: "Jingkou and Caishi are both vital; each needs five thousand crack troops and two hundred Golden Wing ships patrolling the river."

sentences.zh: 憲及驃騎將軍蕭摩訶皆為以然，乃與文武群臣共議，請如毅策。

translations.literal: Xian and the Flying Cavalry General Xiao Mohe both thought it so; they then discussed the matter jointly with civil and military ministers and requested that Yi's plan be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian and Flying Cavalry General Xiao Mohe agreed; they took the proposal to the full court and asked that Fan Yi's plan be adopted.

sentences.zh: 施文慶恐無兵從己，廢其述職，而客卿又利文慶之任，己得專權，俱言於朝曰：「必有論義，不假面陳；

translations.literal: Shi Wenqing feared that if troops were sent he would have none to follow him and would lose his chance to take office, and Keqing also favored Wenqing's appointment so that he himself could monopolize power; both said at court: "If there must be debate, there is no need to report in person;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wenqing feared that dispatching troops would leave him none to command and cost him his new post; Keqing, wanting Wenqing gone so he could rule alone, joined him at court in saying: "If debate is needed, there is no need to appear in person;

sentences.zh: 但作文啟，即為通奏。」

translations.literal: simply write a memorial and it will be passed up for report."
translations.idiomatic: write a memorial and it will reach the throne."

sentences.zh: 憲等以為然，二人繼啟入，白帝曰：「此是常事，邊城將帥足以當之。

translations.literal: Xian and the others thought it so; the two men successively submitted memorials and told the emperor: "This is an ordinary matter; the border generals are sufficient to meet it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian and the others agreed; the two men sent memorial after memorial telling the emperor: "This is routine; frontier commanders can handle it.

sentences.zh: 若出人船，必恐驚擾。」

translations.literal: If ships and men are sent out, it will surely cause alarm and disturbance."
translations.idiomatic: Sending out ships and troops will only spread panic."

sentences.zh: 及隋軍臨江，間諜驟至，憲等殷勤奏請，至於再三。

translations.literal: When the Sui army reached the Yangtze, spies arrived in sudden succession; Xian and the others earnestly memorialized and requested action, even to the point of doing so again and again.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui army reached the Yangtze, reports flooded in; Yuan Xian and his allies pleaded urgently again and again.

sentences.zh: 文慶曰：「元會將逼，南郊之日，太子多從；

translations.literal: Wenqing said: "The New Year's assembly is pressing, and on the day of the Southern Suburb sacrifice the crown prince will largely accompany the rites;
translations.idiomatic: Wenqing said: "The New Year's court is at hand, and on the day of the Southern Suburb rites the crown prince must attend;

sentences.zh: 今若出兵，事便廢闕。」

translations.literal: if troops are sent out now, the ceremonies will be broken off."
translations.idiomatic: if we mobilize now the ceremonies will be ruined."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「今且出兵，若北邊無事，因以水軍從郊，何為不可！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "For now send out troops; if nothing happens on the northern frontier, then let the navy follow to the suburban sacrifice—why should that be impossible!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Mobilize for now; if the north stays quiet, the fleet can still join the suburban rites—why not?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「如此則聲聞鄰境，便謂國弱。」

translations.literal: Wenqing again said: "If it is done this way, word will reach neighboring states and they will say the realm is weak.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqing added: "Word will reach our neighbors and they will call the realm weak.

sentences.zh: 後又以貨動江總，總內為之遊說。

translations.literal: Later they again used gifts to sway Jiang Zong, and Zong inwardly lobbied on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: They then bribed Jiang Zong, who pressed their case within the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝重違其意，而迫群官之請，乃令付外詳議。

translations.literal: The emperor was loath to go against their wishes, yet pressed by the officials' requests, he then ordered the matter handed to the outer court for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hated to cross them, but under pressure from the officials he referred the matter to the outer court for full debate.

sentences.zh: 總又抑憲等，由是議久不決。

translations.literal: Zong again suppressed Xian and the others, and by this the deliberation long went undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zong again blocked Yuan Xian and his allies, and the debate dragged on without resolution.

sentences.zh: 帝從容謂侍臣曰：「王氣在此。

translations.literal: The emperor said leisurely to his attendants: "The royal aura is here.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his attendants at ease: "Imperial fortune rests here.

sentences.zh: 齊兵三來，周師再來，無不摧敗。

translations.literal: Qi armies came three times and Zhou armies came twice, and without exception they were crushed and defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Qi invaded three times and Zhou twice, and each time they were shattered.

sentences.zh: 彼何為者邪！」

translations.literal: What are they trying to do!"
translations.idiomatic: What can they hope to do?"

sentences.zh: 都官尚書孔范曰：「長江天塹，古以為限隔南北，今日虜軍豈能飛渡邪！

translations.literal: The Minister of Justice Kong Fan said: "The Yangtze River is a heavenly moat; since antiquity it has been thought to divide north and south—how can the barbarian army today fly across it!
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Kong Fan said: "The Yangtze is Heaven's moat, the ancient boundary between north and south—can the northern army fly across it?

sentences.zh: 邊將欲作功勞，妄言事急。

translations.literal: The border generals want to make achievements and falsely say the matter is urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier commanders crave glory and cry wolf.

sentences.zh: 臣每患官卑，虜若渡江，臣定作太尉公矣！」

translations.literal: I have always regretted my low rank; if the barbarians cross the river, I am sure to become Grand Commandant Duke!"
translations.idiomatic: I have always regretted my humble rank—if they cross the river I shall surely be made Grand Commandant Duke!"

sentences.zh: 或妄言北軍馬死，范曰：「此是我馬，何為而死！」

translations.literal: Someone falsely reported that the northern army's horses were dying; Fan said: "Those are my horses—why should they die!"
translations.idiomatic: When someone claimed the northern horses were dying, Fan said: "Those are my horses—why should they die?"

sentences.zh: 帝笑以為然，故不為深備，奏伎、縱酒、賦詩不輟。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and thought it so, and therefore did not make deep preparations; he kept presenting entertainers, indulging in wine, and composing poetry without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and agreed, and so made no serious defense; he kept up music, feasting, and verse without pause.

sentences.zh: 7是歲，吐谷渾裨王拓跋木彌請以千餘家降隋。

translations.literal: 7 That year, the Tuyuhun subordinate king Tuoba Mimi requested to surrender to Sui with more than one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: 7 That year Tuoba Mimi, a Tuyuhun subordinate prince, asked to surrender to Sui with more than a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 隋主曰：「溥天之下，皆是朕臣，朕之撫育，俱存仁孝。

translations.literal: The Sui emperor said: "All under broad Heaven are my subjects; in my nurturing care I preserve benevolence and filial piety alike.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor said: "All under Heaven are my subjects; I nurture them all in benevolence and duty.

sentences.zh: 渾賊惛狂，妻子懷怖，並思歸化，自救危亡。

translations.literal: The Hun bandits are maddened and reckless; wives and children live in fear and all think to return and submit, to save themselves from peril and death.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun king runs mad; wives and children tremble and long to come home and save themselves.

sentences.zh: 然叛夫背父，不可收納。

translations.literal: Yet a man who betrays his lord and turns against his father cannot be received and admitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a traitor who turns against his lord and kin cannot simply be welcomed.

sentences.zh: 又其本意正自避死，今若違拒，又復不仁。

translations.literal: Moreover, their original intent was precisely to escape death; if we now refuse and reject them, that again would be unbenevolent.
translations.idiomatic: Their aim is only to live; to turn them away now would be cruel.

sentences.zh: 若更有音信，但宜慰撫，任其自拔，不須出兵應接。

translations.literal: If further word comes, we should only comfort and soothe them, let them come out on their own, and need not send troops to meet and support them.
translations.idiomatic: If more word comes, comfort them and let them flee on their own; do not send troops to meet them.

sentences.zh: 其妹夫及甥欲來，亦任其意，不勞勸誘也。」

translations.literal: If their brothers-in-law and nephews wish to come, likewise let their intent prevail; there is no need to labor at persuasion and enticement."
translations.idiomatic: If brothers-in-law and nephews wish to come, let them; do not press them."

sentences.zh: 8河南王移茲裒卒，隋主令其弟樹歸襲統其眾。

translations.literal: 8 The Henan King Yizibei died; the Sui emperor ordered his younger brother Shugui to succeed and take command of his followers.
translations.idiomatic: 8 When Henan King Yizibei died, the Sui emperor had his younger brother Shugui succeed him and take command of his people.
